value.zh: 儁生京兆尹防，字建公。
value.en: Jun’s son was Fang, governor of Jingzhao, courtesy name Jiangong.
value.literal: Jun fathered Governor of the Metropolitan Region Fang, courtesy name Jiangong.

value.zh: 帝即防之第二子也。
value.en: He was the second son of Fang.
value.literal: The Emperor was Fang’s second son.

value.zh: 少有奇節，聰朗多大略，博學洽聞，伏膺儒教。
value.en: Even young he revealed unusual steadfastness—acute, far-sighted, erudite, and steeped in the Confucian canon.
value.literal: In youth he showed uncommon integrity; he was bright and broad in strategic grasp, widely read and well informed, and devoted himself to Confucian teaching.

value.zh: 漢末大亂，常慨然有憂天下心。
value.en: As Han unraveled, he was repeatedly consumed by anxiety for the empire.
value.literal: At the end of Han, when great turmoil arose, he often felt stirred with concern for the realm.

value.zh: 南陽太守同郡楊俊名知人，[1]見帝，未弱冠，以為非常之器。
value.en: Yang Jun of Nanyang—his fellow townsman and a celebrated judge of talent—met him before his cap-and-girdle ceremony and pronounced him a figure of rare promise.
value.literal: Yang Jun of the same commandery, prefect of Nanyang, famed for judging men,[1] met the Emperor before his twentieth year and deemed him an extraordinary vessel.

value.zh: 尚書清河崔琰與帝兄朗善，亦謂朗曰：「君弟聰亮明允，剛斷英特，非子所及也。」
value.en: Cui Yan of Qinghe, who served in the Secretariat, was close to his elder brother Sima Lang and told Lang, “Your brother combines lucidity with integrity and carries an iron decisiveness—you cannot rival him.”
value.literal: Minister Cui Yan of Qinghe was on good terms with the Emperor’s elder brother Lang and also said to Lang, “Your younger brother is clear-sighted and fair-minded, resolute and extraordinary—not someone you can match.”

value.zh: 漢建安六年，郡舉上計掾。
value.en: In Han’s sixth Jian’an year the commandery recommended him as clerk for the capital assessment.
value.literal: In the sixth year of Jian’an of Han, the commandery nominated him as clerk for the annual accounts.

value.zh: 魏武帝為司空，聞而辟之。
value.en: Cao Cao, then minister of works, heard of him and summoned him to service.
value.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei was Minister of Works and, hearing of him, summoned him.

value.zh: 帝知漢運方微，不欲屈節曹氏，辭以風痹，不能起居。
value.en: Knowing the Han house was in decline, he refused to bend himself to the Cao clan and pleaded crippling wind paralysis that kept him from rising.
value.literal: The Emperor knew Han’s mandate was failing and did not wish to bend his integrity to the Cao house; he declined on the grounds of wind paralysis and inability to rise.

value.zh: 魏武使人夜往密刺之，帝堅臥不動。
value.en: Cao Cao sent someone at night to stab him secretly, but Sima Yi lay rigidly in bed and did not move.
value.literal: Emperor Wu sent someone by night to stab him secretly; the Emperor lay rigid and did not move.

value.zh: 及魏武為丞相，又辟為文學掾，敕行者曰：「若復盤桓，便收之。」
value.en: When Cao Cao became Chancellor he summoned him again as literary clerk and told the courier, “If he hesitates once more, seize him.”
value.literal: When Emperor Wu became Chancellor, he again summoned him as clerk for literature and instructed the messenger: “If he stalls again, arrest him.”

value.zh: 帝懼而就職。
value.en: Terrified, he accepted the appointment.
value.literal: The Emperor, in fear, took the post.

value.zh: 於是使與太子游處，遷黃門侍郎，轉議郎、丞相東曹屬，尋轉主簿。
value.en: Thereafter he was assigned to attend the crown prince, promoted to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates, transferred to Consultant and then aide in the Chancellor's Eastern Bureau, and soon made chief clerk.
value.literal: Thereafter he was assigned to attend the crown prince, promoted to Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gates, transferred to Consultant and then aide in the Chancellor's Eastern Bureau, and soon made chief clerk.

value.zh: 從討張魯，言於魏武曰：「劉備以詐力虜劉璋，蜀人未附而遠爭江陵，此機不可失也。
value.en: On the expedition against Zhang Lu he urged Cao Cao: “Liu Bei bullied his way into Yi through trickery; the Shu populace still mistrusts him while he reaches for Jiangling—do not let this opening slip.
value.literal: Accompanying the campaign against Zhang Lu, he said to Emperor Wu, “Liu Bei seized Liu Zhang by deceit and force; the people of Shu are not yet attached, yet he contests Jiangling from afar—this opportunity must not be missed.

value.zh: 今若曜威漢中，益州震動，進兵臨之，勢必瓦解。
value.en: Show strength in Hanzhong and Yi province will reel; press forward and their front will collapse.
value.literal: If we now display our might in Hanzhong, Yizhou will be shaken; advance the army against it and it will surely crumble.

value.zh: 因此之勢，易為功力。
value.en: Ride that tide and the task becomes straightforward.
value.literal: Riding this momentum, success will come easily.

value.zh: 聖人不能違時，亦不失時矣。」
value.en: Even the sage neither fights the moment nor lets it pass unused.”
value.literal: The sage cannot defy the hour, yet neither does he miss it.”

value.zh: 魏武曰：「人苦無足，既得隴右，復欲得蜀！」
value.en: Cao Cao replied, “People are never satisfied—take Longyou and they hunger for Shu!”
value.literal: Emperor Wu said, “Men suffer from insatiable greed—having gained Longyou, they want Shu too!”

value.zh: 言竟不從。
value.en: He would not take the counsel.
value.literal: In the end he did not follow the advice.

value.zh: 既而從討孫權，破之。
value.en: He later joined the campaign against Sun Quan and helped rout him.
value.literal: He then accompanied the campaign against Sun Quan and defeated him.

value.zh: 軍還，權遣使乞降，上表稱臣，陳說天命。
value.en: On the army’s return Sun Quan sent envoys suing for peace, presented a memorial as a vassal, and rehearsed Heaven’s mandate.
value.literal: When the army returned, Sun Quan sent envoys begging to surrender, submitted a memorial declaring himself a subject, and expounded the mandate of Heaven.

value.zh: 魏武帝曰：「此兒欲踞吾著爐炭上邪！」
value.en: Cao Cao snapped, “Does that boy mean to roast me over live coals?”
value.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei said, “Does this fellow want to seat me on coals over a furnace?”

value.zh: 答曰：「漢運垂終，殿下十分天下而有其九，以服事之。
value.en: He answered: “The Han flame gutters while you hold nine parts in ten yet still bow to the emperor.
value.literal: He replied: “Han’s mandate is near its end; Your Highness holds nine-tenths of the realm yet still serves it.

value.zh: 權之稱臣，天人之意也。
value.en: Sun Quan’s offer to submit answers both Heaven and the human heart.
value.literal: Sun Quan’s submission accords with the will of Heaven and men.

value.zh: 虞、夏、殷、周不以謙讓者，畏天知命也。」
value.en: The sage-kings of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou yielded not from timidity but because they revered Heaven and accepted its mandate.”
value.literal: Yu, Xia, Yin, and Zhou did not yield out of mere modesty—they feared Heaven and knew the mandate.”

value.zh: 魏國既建，遷太子中庶子。
value.en: Once the Wei kingdom was founded he rose to palace attendant to the heir apparent.
value.literal: When the state of Wei was established, he was promoted to palace attendant to the heir apparent.

value.zh: 每與大謀，輒有奇策，為太子所信重，與陳羣、吳質、朱鑠號曰四友。
value.en: In every grand council he supplied sharp schemes; the heir relied on him and paired him with Chen Qun, Wu Zhi, and Zhu Shuo as the “Four Friends.”
value.literal: Whenever major plans were laid he produced striking stratagems; the heir trusted and esteemed him, and with Chen Qun, Wu Zhi, and Zhu Shuo he was called the Four Friends.

value.zh: 遷為軍司馬，言於魏武曰：「昔箕子陳謀，以食為首。
value.en: Promoted army marshal, he told Cao Cao: “When Jizi advised the king, grain came first.
value.literal: He was promoted to army marshal and said to Emperor Wu, “When Jizi presented his counsel, he put food first.

value.zh: 今天下不耕者蓋二十餘萬，非經國遠籌也。
value.en: Today more than two hundred thousand people are not farming; that is no long-range plan for governing the state.
value.literal: Today perhaps two hundred thousand men do not till the soil—this is no far-reaching policy for governing the state.

value.zh: 雖戎甲未卷，自宜且耕且守。」
value.en: Even while armor has not yet been put away, we should farm and defend at the same time.”
value.literal: Though armor is not yet laid aside, we should farm and defend at the same time.”

value.zh: 魏武納之，於是務農積穀，國用豐贍。
value.en: Cao Cao agreed; farming and granaries were stressed until state stores overflowed.
value.literal: Emperor Wu accepted this; agriculture was emphasized and grain stored, and state supplies grew ample.

value.zh: 帝又言荊州刺史胡脩粗暴，南鄉太守傅方驕奢，並不可居邊。
value.en: He further warned that Hu Xiu, inspector of Jingzhou, was brutish and Fu Fang, prefect of Nanxiang, was decadent—neither belonged on the border.
value.literal: The Emperor also said that Hu Xiu, inspector of Jingzhou, was brutal and coarse, and Fu Fang, prefect of Nanxiang, arrogant and extravagant—neither was fit to hold the frontier.

value.zh: 魏武不之察。
value.en: Cao Cao brushed the warning aside.
value.literal: Emperor Wu did not heed him.

value.zh: 及蜀將關羽圍曹仁於樊，于禁等七軍皆沒，脩、方果降羽，而仁圍甚急焉。
value.en: When Guan Yu of Shu penned Cao Ren at Fan and Yu Jin’s seven corps vanished beneath the flood, Hu Xiu and Fu Fang duly defected to Guan Yu and the siege of Fan tightened unbearably.
value.literal: When Shu general Guan Yu besieged Cao Ren at Fan and Yu Jin’s seven armies were drowned, Hu and Fu indeed surrendered to Guan Yu, and Ren’s siege grew desperate.

value.zh: 是時漢帝都許昌，魏武以為近賊，欲徙河北。
value.en: The Han emperor still sat at Xuchang; Cao Cao judged it perilously near the foe and planned to shift the court north of the river.
value.literal: At that time the Han emperor was at Xuchang; Emperor Wu thought it too close to the enemy and wished to move the capital north of the Yellow River.

value.zh: 帝諫曰：「禁等為水所沒，非戰守之所失，於國家大計未有所損，而便遷都，既示敵以弱，又淮沔之人大不安矣。
value.en: He objected: “Yu Jin’s men drowned—they were not routed in the field. The empire’s strategy is intact; relocating now advertises fear and panics everyone between the Huai and the Han.
value.literal: The Emperor remonstrated: “Yu Jin and the others were lost to water, not to defeat in battle or defense—the state’s grand plan is not yet harmed. To move the capital rashly would show weakness to the enemy and greatly unsettle the people between the Huai and the Han.

value.zh: 孫權、劉備，外親內疏，羽之得意，權所不願也。
value.en: Sun Quan and Liu Bei are allies in name alone; Sun Quan cannot relish Guan Yu’s triumph.
value.literal: Sun Quan and Liu Bei are outward kin but inwardly estranged; Guan Yu’s triumph is not what Quan desires.

value.zh: 可喻權所，令掎其後，則樊圍自解。」
value.en: Urge Sun Quan to stab Guan Yu in the rear and the ring around Fan loosens on its own.”
value.literal: You may instruct Quan to strike Guan Yu from behind; then the siege of Fan will lift of itself.”

value.zh: 魏武從之。
value.en: Cao Cao adopted the plan.
value.literal: Emperor Wu followed this advice.

value.zh: 權果遣將呂蒙西襲公安，拔之，羽遂為蒙所獲。
value.en: Sun Quan dispatched Lü Meng westward against Gong’an, seized it, and Guan Yu fell into Meng’s hands.
value.literal: Quan indeed sent general Lü Meng to raid Gong’an from the west and took it; Guan Yu was then captured by Meng.

value.zh: 魏武以荊州遺黎及屯田在潁川者逼近南寇，[2]皆欲徙之。
value.en: Cao Cao meant to uproot the leftover households of Jingzhou and the military colonies in Yingchuan because both fronts skirted the southern enemy.
value.literal: Emperor Wu wished to relocate the remnant people of Jingzhou and the agricultural colonies in Yingchuan because they lay close to the southern foe.

value.zh: 帝曰：「荊楚輕脫，易動難安。
value.en: He replied, “The Jing-Chu folk are restless—quick to bolt and slow to reassure.
value.literal: The Emperor said, “The people of Jing-Chu are flighty—easy to stir, hard to settle.

value.zh: 關羽新破，諸為惡者藏竄觀望。
value.en: Guan Yu’s fall leaves malcontents skulking in the shadows, watching.
value.literal: Guan Yu has just been defeated; those who meant harm hide and watch.

value.zh: 今徙其善者，既傷其意，將令去者不敢復還。」
value.en: Uproot the loyal now and you crush their hearts; refugees will never dare come home.”
value.literal: If we now relocate the good among them, we wound their feelings and will make those who flee dare not return.”

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: Cao Cao relented.
value.literal: [Emperor Wu] followed this.

value.zh: 其後諸亡者悉復業。
value.en: Later every exile drifted back to his fields.
value.literal: Afterwards all who had fled resumed their occupations.

value.zh: 及魏武薨于洛陽，朝野危懼。
value.en: When Cao Cao died at Luoyang, court and capital trembled.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu died at Luoyang, court and countryside were fearful.

value.zh: 帝綱紀喪事，內外肅然。
value.en: He imposed discipline on the mourning rites until palace and province stood calm.
value.literal: The Emperor directed the funeral rites; within and without there was solemn order.

value.zh: 乃奉梓宮還鄴。
value.en: He convoyed the royal catafalque back to Ye.
value.literal: He then escorted the coffin back to Ye.

value.zh: 魏文帝即位，封河津亭侯，轉丞相長史。
value.en: When Emperor Wen of Wei ascended the throne, Sima Yi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hejin Village and transferred to be chief clerk to the chancellor.
value.literal: When Emperor Wen of Wei ascended the throne, Sima Yi was enfeoffed as Marquis of Hejin Village and transferred to be chief clerk to the chancellor.

value.zh: 會孫權帥兵西過，朝議以樊、襄陽無穀，不可以禦寇。
value.en: At the time, Sun Quan led troops westward. Court discussion held that Fan and Xiangyang had no grain and could not be used to resist the invaders.
value.literal: At the time, Sun Quan led troops westward. Court discussion held that Fan and Xiangyang had no grain and could not be used to resist the invaders.

value.zh: 時曹仁鎮襄陽，請召仁還宛。
value.en: At the time Cao Ren was stationed at Xiangyang, and they requested that Ren be summoned back to Wan.
value.literal: At the time Cao Ren was stationed at Xiangyang, and they requested that Ren be summoned back to Wan.

value.zh: 帝曰：「孫權新破關羽，此其欲自結之時也，必不敢為患。襄陽水陸之衝，禦寇要害，不可棄也。」
value.en: The emperor said, "Sun Quan has only just defeated Guan Yu; this is the moment when he wants to secure his own position, and he certainly will not dare become a menace. Xiangyang is a crossing point for water and land routes and a vital place for resisting invaders; it cannot be abandoned."
value.literal: The emperor said, "Sun Quan has only just defeated Guan Yu; this is the moment when he wants to secure his own position, and he certainly will not dare become a menace. Xiangyang is a crossing point for water and land routes and a vital place for resisting invaders; it cannot be abandoned."

value.zh: 言竟不從。
value.en: In the end, his words were not followed.
value.literal: In the end, his words were not followed.

value.zh: 仁遂焚棄二城，權果不為寇，魏文悔之。
value.en: Ren accordingly burned and abandoned the two cities. Quan indeed did not invade, and Emperor Wen of Wei regretted it.
value.literal: Ren accordingly burned and abandoned the two cities. Quan indeed did not invade, and Emperor Wen of Wei regretted it.

value.zh: 及魏受漢禪，以帝為尚書。
value.en: When Wei received Han's abdication, the emperor was made minister in the Secretariat.
value.literal: When Wei received Han's abdication, the emperor was made minister in the Secretariat.

value.zh: 頃之，轉督軍、御史中丞，封安國鄉侯。
value.en: Before long, he was transferred to be army supervisor and palace aide to the censor-in-chief, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anguo Township.
value.literal: Before long, he was transferred to be army supervisor and palace aide to the censor-in-chief, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Anguo Township.

value.zh: 黃初二年，督軍官罷，遷侍中、尚書右僕射。
value.en: In Huangchu’s second year the army-supervisor post was scrapped; he became palace attendant and right vice director of the Secretariat.
value.literal: In the second year of Huangchu (221), the office of supervisor of armies was abolished; he was promoted to palace attendant and right vice director of the Secretariat.

value.zh: 五年，天子南巡，觀兵吳疆。
value.en: In the fifth year the emperor toured south and drilled troops along Wu’s frontier.
value.literal: In the fifth year (224), the Son of Heaven toured south and reviewed troops on Wu’s border.

value.zh: 帝留鎮許昌，改封向鄉侯，轉撫軍、假節，領兵五千，加給事中、錄尚書事。
value.en: He stayed to hold Xuchang, was re-enfeoffed as marquis of Xiang township, promoted Protector of the Army with credential axe, led five thousand soldiers, and added duties as palace attendant and overseer of Secretariat business.
value.literal: The Emperor remained to guard Xuchang, was enfeoffed as marquis of Xiang township, became Protector of the Army with ceremonial axe, commanded five thousand troops, and was given concurrent posts as attendant within the palace and recorder of Secretariat affairs.

value.zh: 帝固辭。
value.en: He firmly declined.
value.literal: The Emperor firmly declined.

value.zh: 天子曰：「吾於庶事，以夜繼晝，無須臾寧息。
value.en: The emperor said, “I chase paperwork from dusk to dawn without a breath’s pause.
value.literal: The Son of Heaven said, “In routine affairs I follow night with day without a moment’s rest.

value.zh: 此非以為榮，乃分憂耳。」
value.en: That burden is not glory—it is sharing the weight on my shoulders.”
value.literal: This is not for honor—it is to share my burdens.”

value.zh: 六年，天子復大興舟師征吳，復命帝居守，內鎮百姓，外供軍資。
value.en: The sixth year brought another massive river expedition against Wu; again he was told to stay behind—steady the interior and provision the campaign.
value.literal: In the sixth year (225), the Son of Heaven again raised a great fleet to campaign against Wu and again ordered the Emperor to remain as guardian—pacifying the people within and supplying the army without.

value.zh: 臨行，詔曰：「吾深以後事為念，故以委卿。
value.en: Before embarking he proclaimed: “I brood over what follows my reign—so I lay it in your hands.
value.literal: On departure he issued an edict: “I think deeply on what comes after me; therefore I entrust you.

value.zh: 曹參雖有戰功，而蕭何為重。
value.en: Cao Shen won battles, yet Xiao He anchored the state.
value.literal: Cao Shen had battle merit, yet Xiao He mattered more.

value.zh: 使吾無西顧之憂，不亦可乎！」
value.en: Free my mind from the western march—is that too much to ask!”
value.literal: Let me have no worry over the west—is that not enough!”

value.zh: 天子自廣陵還洛陽，詔帝曰：「吾東，撫軍當總西事；
value.en: Returning from Guangling to Luoyang he decreed: “When I march east, the Protector commands the west;
value.literal: When the Son of Heaven returned from Guangling to Luoyang, he issued an edict to the Emperor: “When I am east, the Protector of the Army shall oversee the west;

value.zh: 吾西，撫軍當總東事。」
value.en: when I march west, the Protector commands the east.”
value.literal: when I am west, the Protector of the Army shall oversee the east.”

value.zh: 於是帝留鎮許昌。
value.en: So he continued to anchor Xuchang.
value.literal: Thereupon the Emperor remained to guard Xuchang.

value.zh: 及天子疾篤，帝與曹真、陳羣等見於崇華殿之南堂，並受顧命輔政。
value.en: When the Son of Heaven became gravely ill, the emperor, Cao Zhen, Chen Qun, and others met him in the south hall of Chonghua Palace and together received his final charge to assist in government.
value.literal: When the Son of Heaven became gravely ill, the emperor, Cao Zhen, Chen Qun, and others met him in the south hall of Chonghua Palace and together received his final charge to assist in government.

value.zh: 詔太子曰：「有間此三公者，慎勿疑之。」
value.en: He instructed the crown prince, saying, "If anyone sows discord against these three lords, be careful not to doubt them."
value.literal: He instructed the crown prince, saying, "If anyone sows discord against these three lords, be careful not to doubt them."

value.zh: 明帝即位，改封舞陽侯。
value.en: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Sima Yi's enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Wuyang.
value.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Sima Yi's enfeoffment was changed to Marquis of Wuyang.

value.zh: 及孫權圍江夏，遣其將諸葛瑾、張霸并攻襄陽，帝督諸軍討權，走之。
value.en: When Sun Quan invested Jiangxia and Zhuge Jin with Zhang Ba struck Xiangyang together, he led the host against Sun Quan and threw him back.
value.literal: When Sun Quan besieged Jiangxia and sent his generals Zhuge Jin and Zhang Ba jointly to attack Xiangyang, the Emperor commanded the armies against Quan and drove him off.

value.zh: 進擊，敗瑾，斬霸，并首級千餘。
value.en: He pressed the pursuit, routed Zhuge Jin, slew Zhang Ba, and piled up more than a thousand heads.
value.literal: Pressing the attack, he defeated Jin, beheaded Ba, and took over a thousand heads.

value.zh: 遷驃騎將軍。
value.en: He was elevated to general of the agile cavalry.
value.literal: He was promoted to general of agile cavalry.

value.zh: 太和元年六月，天子詔帝屯于宛，加督荊、豫二州諸軍事。
value.en: In the sixth month of the first year of Taihe (227), the Son of Heaven ordered the emperor to garrison at Wan and additionally placed him in command of military affairs in Jing and Yu provinces.
value.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Taihe (227), the Son of Heaven ordered the emperor to garrison at Wan and additionally placed him in command of military affairs in Jing and Yu provinces.

value.zh: 初，蜀將孟達之降也，魏朝遇之甚厚。
value.en: Earlier, when Shu’s general Meng Da defected, Wei showered him with favor.
value.literal: Earlier, when Shu general Meng Da had surrendered, the Wei court treated him generously.

value.zh: 帝以達言行傾巧不可任，驟諫不見聽，乃以達領新城太守，封侯，假節。
value.en: He judged Da’s tongue treacherous and untrustworthy; repeated remonstrance failed, so Da received acting prefect of Xincheng, a marquisate, and the credential axe.
value.literal: The Emperor deemed Da’s words and conduct slippery and unreliable; though he remonstrated repeatedly he was not heard, and Da was made acting prefect of Xincheng, enfeoffed as a marquis, and given the ceremonial axe.

value.zh: 達於是連吳固蜀，潛圖中國。
value.en: Da then stitched Wu to Shu and schemed against the heartland in secret.
value.literal: Da then allied with Wu and Shu and secretly plotted against the central plains.

value.zh: 蜀相諸葛亮惡其反覆，又慮其為患。
value.en: Zhuge Liang despised his flip-flopping and dreaded the chaos he might unleash.
value.literal: Shu’s chancellor Zhuge Liang despised his vacillation and also feared he would cause trouble.

value.zh: 達與魏興太守申儀有隙，亮欲促其事，乃遣郭模詐降，過儀，因漏泄其謀。
value.en: Da quarrelled with Shen Yi of Weixing; Liang hurried matters by sending Guo Mo under false colors past Yi to spill the conspiracy.
value.literal: Da had a rift with Shen Yi, prefect of Weixing; Liang wished to hasten matters and sent Guo Mo feigning surrender, who passed through Yi and leaked the plot.

value.zh: 達聞其謀漏泄，將舉兵。
value.en: Once Da learned the secret was out, he prepared to rebel.
value.literal: When Da heard his plot had leaked, he prepared to rise in arms.

value.zh: 帝恐達速發，以書喻之曰：「將軍昔棄劉備，託身國家，國家委將軍以疆埸之任，任將軍以圖蜀之事，可謂心貫白日。
value.en: Fearing a swift rising, he wrote: “You abandoned Liu Bei for us; we placed the border in your hands and tasked you with Shu—your loyalty blazes like noon.
value.literal: The Emperor feared Da would move quickly and wrote to him: “General, you once abandoned Liu Bei and entrusted yourself to the state; the state entrusted you with the frontier and charged you with planning against Shu—your heart may be said to pierce the bright sun.

value.zh: 蜀人愚智，莫不切齒於將軍。
value.en: Every Shu soul, wise or dull, grinds teeth at your name.
value.literal: Wise or foolish, everyone in Shu gnashes teeth at you.

value.zh: 諸葛亮欲相破，惟苦無路耳。
value.en: Zhuge Liang longs to ruin you yet lacked a lever until now.
value.literal: Zhuge Liang wishes to destroy you but only lacks the means.

value.zh: 模之所言，非小事也，亮豈輕之而令宣露，此殆易知耳。」
value.en: Mo’s tale is no gossip—would Zhuge Liang broadcast it carelessly? The answer is plain.”
value.literal: What Mo said is no trifle—would Liang treat it lightly and let it spread? This is easy to see.”

value.zh: 達得書大喜，猶與不決。
value.en: Da read the letter with delight yet still wavered.
value.literal: Da received the letter and was greatly pleased, yet still hesitated.

value.zh: 帝乃潛軍進討。
value.en: He then stole forward with the army.
value.literal: The Emperor then secretly advanced to attack.

value.zh: 諸將言達與二賊交構，宜觀望而後動。
value.en: His officers argued Da colluded with both enemies and urged caution.
value.literal: The generals said Da was in league with the two foes and they should watch and wait before acting.

value.zh: 帝曰：「達無信義，此其相疑之時也，當及其未定促決之。」
value.en: He said, “Da knows no loyalty—this is the hour of mutual doubt; strike before his camp steadies.”
value.literal: The Emperor said, “Da lacks good faith; this is when mutual suspicion reigns—we must strike before he is settled.”

value.zh: 乃倍道兼行，八日到其城下。
value.en: He forced the march and reached the walls in eight days.
value.literal: He therefore doubled the march and in eight days reached the walls.

value.zh: 吳蜀各遣其將向西城安橋、木闌塞以救達，帝分諸將以距之。
value.en: Wu and Shu each rushed columns toward Xicheng, An Bridge, and Mulansai to rescue Da; he split commands to intercept them.
value.literal: Wu and Shu each sent generals toward Xicheng, Anqiao, and Mulansai to relieve Da; the Emperor divided his generals to block them.

value.zh: 初，達與亮書曰：「宛去洛八百里，去吾一千二百里，聞吾舉事，當表上天子，比相反覆，一月間也，則吾城已固，諸軍足辦。
value.en: Da once wrote Zhuge Liang: “Wan lies eight hundred li from Luoyang and twelve hundred from me; were I to rebel, Luoyang must memorialize the throne—round-trip paperwork eats a month; by then my walls would stand firm and my troops ready.
value.literal: Earlier Da had written to Liang: “Wan is eight hundred li from Luoyang and twelve hundred from me; when I rise, [the court] must memorialize the Son of Heaven—by the time reports go back and forth a month will have passed; then my city will be secure and my forces ready.

value.zh: 則吾所在深險，司馬公必不自來；
value.en: My terrain is rugged and remote—Lord Sima will never march in person;
value.literal: My position is deep and defensible; Lord Sima will surely not come himself;

value.zh: 諸將來，吾無患矣。」
value.en: if only subordinates arrive I need not worry.”
value.literal: if only his generals come, I have nothing to fear.”

value.zh: 及兵到，達又告亮曰：「吾舉事八日，而兵至城下，何其神速也！」
value.en: When the army appeared Da wired Liang: “Eight days into my rising and they ring my walls—what speed!”
value.literal: When the troops arrived, Da told Liang: “I rose eight days ago and already troops are at my walls—how swift!”

value.zh: 上庸城三面阻水，達於城外為木柵以自固。
value.en: Shangyong hugged water on three faces; Da threw up timber palisades beyond the walls.
value.literal: Shangyong was bounded by water on three sides; Da built a wooden palisade outside the city to fortify himself.

value.zh: [3]帝渡水，破其柵，直造城下。
value.en: [3] He forded the streams, smashed the stockade, and drove to the moat.
value.literal: [3] The Emperor crossed the water, broke the palisade, and came straight to the foot of the walls.

value.zh: 八道攻之，旬有六日，達甥鄧賢、將李輔等開門出降。
value.en: He assaulted along eight avenues; sixteen days later Deng Xian the nephew and general Li Fu opened the gates and capitulated.
value.literal: He attacked from eight directions; after sixteen days Deng Xian, Da’s nephew, and general Li Fu and others opened the gates and surrendered.

value.zh: 斬達，傳首京師。
value.en: They beheaded Meng Da and forwarded his head to Luoyang.
value.literal: Da was executed and his head sent to the capital.

value.zh: 俘獲萬餘人，振旅還于宛。
value.en: They took over ten thousand prisoners and marched back to Wan with drums beating.
value.literal: More than ten thousand captives were taken; the army marched back to Wan in good order.

value.zh: 乃勸農桑，禁浮費，南土悅附焉。
value.en: He urged tillage and silk production, banned needless expense, and the south rallied to him willingly.
value.literal: He then promoted farming and sericulture, forbade wasteful spending, and the southern lands gladly submitted.

value.zh: 初，申儀久在魏興，專威疆埸，輒承制刻印，多所假授。
value.en: Shen Yi had dominated Weixing for years—running the border like a private fief, minting seals without sanction, and handing out titles at will.
value.literal: Earlier, Shen Yi had long held Weixing, arrogated authority along the frontier, repeatedly carved seals on his own authority, and handed out many irregular appointments.

value.zh: 達既誅，有自疑心。
value.en: Once Meng Da fell, Shen Yi began to doubt his own safety.
value.literal: After Da was put to death, Yi grew suspicious of his own position.

value.zh: 時諸郡守以帝新克捷，奉禮求賀，皆聽之。
value.en: County governors arrived with congratulations on his fresh triumph; he received every delegation.
value.literal: At that time the various prefects, because the Emperor had just won a victory, brought gifts seeking congratulation; he accepted them all.

value.zh: 帝使人諷儀，儀至，問承制狀，執之，歸于京師。
value.en: He hinted until Shen Yi appeared at audience, pressed him on those self-made commissions, arrested him, and shipped him east.
value.literal: The Emperor sent someone to sound out Yi; when Yi came to court he questioned him about his unauthorized appointments, seized him, and sent him to the capital.

value.zh: 又徙孟達餘眾七千餘家於幽州。
value.en: He resettled over seven thousand surviving households of Meng Da’s remnant followers in Youzhou.
value.literal: He also relocated more than seven thousand households of Meng Da’s remnant followers to Youzhou.

value.zh: 蜀將姚靜、鄭他等帥其屬七千餘人來降。
value.en: Yao Jing and Zheng Ta of Shu marched in over seven thousand troops to defect.
value.literal: Shu generals Yao Jing and Zheng Ta led their followers—more than seven thousand men—to surrender.

value.zh: 時邊郡新附，多無戶名，魏朝欲加隱實。
value.en: The newly subdued border prefectures still lacked proper household rolls, and the court meant to audit them.
value.literal: At that time the newly annexed marches often lacked registered households, and the Wei court wished to verify them thoroughly.

value.zh: 屬帝朝於京師，天子訪之於帝。
value.en: While he was at audience in Luoyang, the emperor took him aside for advice.
value.literal: When the Emperor attended court in the capital, the Son of Heaven consulted him on the matter.

value.zh: 帝對曰：「賊以密網束下，故下棄之。
value.en: He answered: “Bandits rule through a thousand petty regulations—that is why their subjects flee.
value.literal: The Emperor replied: “The rebels bound their subjects with a harsh net, so the people abandoned them.

value.zh: 宜弘以大綱，則自然安樂。」
value.en: Govern with a loose rein and calm follows without forcing it.”
value.literal: You should rule with a broad policy; then peace will come of itself.”

value.zh: 又問二虜宜討，何者為先？
value.en: The sovereign then asked which foe—Wu or Shu—should come first.
value.literal: He was also asked which of the two enemies ought to be attacked first.

value.zh: 對曰：「吳以中國不習水戰，故敢散居東關。
value.en: He said: “Wu gambles that we fear naval combat, so they string their lines along the eastern passes.
value.literal: He replied: “Wu presumes that the Central Plains do not excel at river warfare, which is why they dare scatter their forces along Dongguan.

value.zh: 凡攻敵，必扼其喉而摏其心。
value.en: Strike always at throat and heart—that is how wars are won.
value.literal: In every attack on an enemy one must seize his throat and strike his heart.

value.zh: 夏口、東關，賊之心喉。
value.en: Xiakou and Dongguan are precisely those vital points.
value.literal: Xiakou and Dongguan are that foe’s heart and throat.

value.zh: 若為陸軍以向皖城，引權東下，為水戰軍向夏口，乘其虛而擊之，此神兵從天而墮，破之必矣。」
value.en: Send infantry toward Wancheng to tug Sun Quan downstream while your fleet thrusts at Xiakou and catches him thin—that is an assault from heaven itself.”
value.literal: If you march a field army toward Wancheng and draw Sun Quan eastward, while a river force pushes toward Xiakou and hits him where he is weak, it will be like heavenly troops falling from the sky—you will surely break him.”

value.zh: 天子並然之，復命帝屯於宛。
value.en: The emperor endorsed it wholeheartedly and told him once more to hold Wan.
value.literal: The Son of Heaven deeply approved and again ordered the Emperor to encamp at Wan.

value.zh: 四年，遷大將軍，加大都督、假黃鉞，與曹真伐蜀。
value.en: Fourth year: he became Grand General and supreme commander with the yellow axe, campaigning beside Cao Zhen against Shu.
value.literal: In the fourth year he was promoted to Grand General, invested as supreme commander-in-chief with the yellow battle-axe, and joined Cao Zhen in campaigning against Shu.

value.zh: 帝自西城斫山開道，水陸並進，泝沔而上，至於朐䏰，拔其新豐縣。
value.en: He hacked a route from Xicheng, drove land and river columns up the Han to Quyu, and seized Xinfeng County.
value.literal: From Xicheng he cut roads through the mountains and advanced by land and water together, moving up the Han River as far as Quyu, where he took Xinfeng County.

value.zh: 軍次丹口，遇雨，班師。
value.en: They paused at Dankou until storms forced a withdrawal.
value.literal: The army halted at Dankou; rain fell and he ordered the troops withdrawn.

value.zh: 是時大修宮室，加之以軍旅，百姓饑弊。
value.en: Court architects ran wild while armies marched—the people starved under both burdens.
value.literal: At that time palace construction was greatly expanded and military campaigns piled on; the common people were hungry and exhausted.

value.zh: 帝將即戎，乃諫曰：「昔周公營洛邑，蕭何造未央，今宮室未備，臣之責也。
value.en: When the emperor was about to go to war, he remonstrated, saying, "In the past, the Duke of Zhou built Luoyi, and Xiao He built Weiyang. Now that the palace buildings are not yet complete, it is my responsibility.
value.literal: When the emperor was about to go to war, he remonstrated, saying, "In the past, the Duke of Zhou built Luoyi, and Xiao He built Weiyang. Now that the palace buildings are not yet complete, it is my responsibility.

value.zh: 然自河以北，百姓困窮，外內有役，勢不並興，宜假絕內務，以救時急。」
value.en: Yet north of the Yellow River, the people are impoverished; there are labor services both outside and inside, and the situation does not allow both to be undertaken at once. The inner works should be temporarily cut off, in order to save the current emergency."
value.literal: Yet north of the Yellow River, the people are impoverished; there are labor services both outside and inside, and the situation does not allow both to be undertaken at once. The inner works should be temporarily cut off, in order to save the current emergency."

value.zh: 景初二年，帥牛金、胡遵等步騎四萬，發自京都。
value.en: Jingchu year two: forty thousand horse and foot under Niu Jin and Hu Zun left Luoyang.
value.literal: In the second year of Jingchu (238) he led Niu Jin, Hu Zun, and others with forty thousand infantry and cavalry out of the capital.

value.zh: 車駕送出西明門，詔弟孚、子師送過溫，賜以穀帛牛酒，敕郡守典農以下皆往會焉。
value.en: The imperial carriage escorted him out through the Ximing Gate; an edict ordered his younger brother Fu and son Shi to see him past Wen, awarding grain, silk, cattle, and wine, and commanded the prefects and agricultural directors downward to assemble.
value.literal: The imperial carriage escorted him through the Ximing Gate; an edict ordered his younger brother Fu and son Shi to see him past Wen, awarding grain, silk, cattle, and wine, and commanded the prefect and agricultural director downward to assemble.

value.zh: 見父老故舊，讌飲累日。
value.en: He lingered with hometown elders over cups for night after night.
value.literal: He met elders and old friends and feasted for days on end.

value.zh: 帝歎息，悵然有感，為歌曰：「天地開闢，日月重光。
value.en: The emperor sighed and, moved with melancholy, made a song, saying, "Heaven and earth opened, sun and moon shone anew.
value.literal: The emperor sighed and, moved with melancholy, made a song, saying, "Heaven and earth opened, sun and moon shone anew.

value.zh: 遭遇際會，畢力遐方。
value.en: Encountering the moment of meeting, I spend all strength in distant regions.
value.literal: Encountering the moment of meeting, I spend all strength in distant regions.

value.zh: 將掃羣穢，還過故鄉。
value.en: I am about to sweep away the massed filth, and on return pass through my old home.
value.literal: I am about to sweep away the massed filth, and on return pass through my old home.

value.zh: 肅清萬里，總齊八荒。
value.en: Purifying ten thousand li, I shall gather and order the eight wastes.
value.literal: Purifying ten thousand li, I shall gather and order the eight wastes.

value.zh: 告成歸老，待罪舞陽。」
value.en: When success is reported, I will return old and await punishment at Wuyang."
value.literal: When success is reported, I will return old and await punishment at Wuyang."

value.zh: 遂進師，經孤竹，越碣石，次于遼水。
value.en: The columns rolled past Guzhu and Jieshi to the Liao.
value.literal: Thereupon he advanced the army, passed Guzhu, crossed Jieshi, and halted at the Liao River.

value.zh: 文懿果遣步騎數萬，阻遼隧，堅壁而守，南北六七十里，以距帝。
value.en: Gongsun Yuan plugged Liaosui with tens of thousands—palisades stretched seventy li along the narrows.
value.literal: Wenyi indeed sent several tens of thousands of infantry and cavalry to block Liaosui, fortifying walls and holding sixty or seventy li north to south against the Emperor.

value.zh: 帝盛兵多張旗幟出其南，賊盡銳赴之。
value.en: Sima Yi feigned strength on the southern bank and drew the Liaodong army off.
value.literal: The Emperor massed troops and unfurled many banners south of them; the rebels committed every elite regiment there.

value.zh: 乃泛舟潛濟以出其北，與賊營相逼，沈舟焚梁，傍遼水作長圍，棄賊而向襄平。
value.en: Under cover of dark water he slipped upstream, burned the crossings, pinned the Liao with earthworks, and ignored the camp for Xiangping.
value.literal: He then floated boats and secretly crossed to their north, pressing against their camp—sank boats, burned bridges, threw a long cordon along the Liao, abandoned the enemy column, and marched on Xiangping.

value.zh: 諸將言曰：「不攻賊而作圍，非所以示眾也。」
value.en: The generals said, "To make a siege without attacking the enemy is not the way to show resolve to the troops."
value.literal: The generals said, "To make a siege without attacking the enemy is not the way to show resolve to the troops."

value.zh: 帝曰：「賊堅營高壘，欲以老吾兵也。
value.en: The emperor said, "The enemy has made a firm camp and high ramparts because he wants to wear out our troops.
value.literal: The emperor said, "The enemy has made a firm camp and high ramparts because he wants to wear out our troops.

value.zh: 攻之，正入其計，此王邑所以恥過昆陽也。
value.en: If we attack it, we fall exactly into his plan; this is why Wang Yi was shamed at Kunyang.
value.literal: If we attack it, we fall exactly into his plan; this is why Wang Yi was shamed at Kunyang.

value.zh: 古人曰，敵雖高壘，不得不與我戰者，攻其所必救也。
value.en: The ancients said that even if the enemy has high ramparts, he cannot avoid fighting us if we attack what he must rescue.
value.literal: The ancients said that even if the enemy has high ramparts, he cannot avoid fighting us if we attack what he must rescue.

value.zh: 賊大眾在此，則巢窟虛矣。
value.en: The enemy's main force is here, so their nest is empty.
value.literal: The enemy's main force is here, so their nest is empty.

value.zh: 我直指襄平，則人懷內懼，懼而求戰，破之必矣。」
value.en: If I point straight at Xiangping, then the people will harbor internal fear; fearing, they will seek battle, and I will certainly defeat them."
value.literal: If I point straight at Xiangping, then the people will harbor internal fear; fearing, they will seek battle, and I will certainly defeat them."

value.zh: 遂整陣而過。
value.en: He aligned divisions and slipped past.
value.literal: Thereupon he dressed ranks and marched through.

value.zh: 賊見兵出其後，果邀之。
value.en: The Liaodong army wheeled about to cut him off.
value.literal: When the rebels saw troops emerge behind them they indeed tried to intercept.

value.zh: 帝謂諸將曰：「所以不攻其營，正欲致此，不可失也。」
value.en: The emperor told the generals, "The reason I did not attack their camp was precisely because I wanted to bring this about. We must not lose it."
value.literal: The emperor told the generals, "The reason I did not attack their camp was precisely because I wanted to bring this about. We must not lose it."

value.zh: 乃縱兵逆擊，大破之，三戰皆捷。
value.en: He hurled the lines forward and routed them thrice running.
value.literal: He then unleashed troops in a counterattack and shattered them; three engagements brought three victories.

value.zh: 賊保襄平，進軍圍之。
value.en: They fled inside Xiangping; he tightened the ring.
value.literal: The rebels held Xiangping; he advanced and invested it.

value.zh: 初，文懿聞魏師之出也，請救於孫權。
value.en: Gongsun Yuan had cried to Sun Quan when Wei stirred.
value.literal: Earlier, when Wenyi heard the Wei army had marched, he begged rescue from Sun Quan.

value.zh: 權亦出兵遙為之聲援，遺文懿書曰：「司馬公善用兵，變化若神，所向無前，深為弟憂之。」
value.en: Quan also sent troops from afar to make a show of support and sent Wenyì a letter, saying, "Sima Gong is good at using troops; his changes are like those of a spirit, and nothing stands before him wherever he turns. I am deeply worried for you, younger brother."
value.literal: Quan also sent troops from afar to make a show of support and sent Wenyì a letter, saying, "Sima Gong is good at using troops; his changes are like those of a spirit, and nothing stands before him wherever he turns. I am deeply worried for you, younger brother."

value.zh: 會霖潦，大水平地數尺，三軍恐，欲移營。
value.en: Monsoon floods drowned the plain; men clamored to move.
value.literal: Seasonal rains poured; floodwaters stood several chi deep on level ground; the three armies feared and wished to shift camp.

value.zh: 帝令軍中敢有言徙者斬。
value.en: He threatened death for talk of redeployment.
value.literal: The Emperor ordered that whoever spoke of relocating be executed.

value.zh: 都督令史張靜犯令，斬之，軍中乃定。
value.en: Zhang Jing broke the rule and lost his head—the ranks fell silent.
value.literal: Supervisory clerk Zhang Jing violated the order and was beheaded—only then did the army steady.

value.zh: 賊恃水，樵牧自若。
value.en: The defenders still sent out woodcutters as if dry.
value.literal: The rebels trusted the water and gathered firewood and grazed cattle as usual.

value.zh: 諸將欲取之，皆不聽。
value.en: Staff urged raids on foragers; he refused each time.
value.literal: The generals wished to seize those parties; he forbade every proposal.

value.zh: 司馬陳珪曰：「昔攻上庸，八部並進，晝夜不息，故能一旬之半，拔堅城，斬孟達。
value.en: Army officer Chen Gui said, "In the past, when we attacked Shangyong, eight divisions advanced together and did not rest day or night; therefore in half a ten-day period we were able to take a firm city and behead Meng Da.
value.literal: Army officer Chen Gui said, "In the past, when we attacked Shangyong, eight divisions advanced together and did not rest day or night; therefore in half a ten-day period we were able to take a firm city and behead Meng Da.

value.zh: 今者遠來而更安緩，愚竊惑焉。」
value.en: Now we have come from afar and instead are calm and slow; foolishly, I am privately puzzled by it."
value.literal: Now we have come from afar and instead are calm and slow; foolishly, I am privately puzzled by it."

value.zh: 帝曰：「孟達眾少而食支一年，吾將士四倍于達而糧不淹月，以一月圖一年，安可不速？
value.en: The emperor said, "Meng Da's men were few, and his food could support a year. My officers and soldiers are four times Da's, but our grain will not last a month. To plan for one year with one month, how could we not be quick?
value.literal: The emperor said, "Meng Da's men were few, and his food could support a year. My officers and soldiers are four times Da's, but our grain will not last a month. To plan for one year with one month, how could we not be quick?

value.zh: 以四擊一，正令半解，猶當為之。
value.en: Using four to attack one, even if half deserted, we still had to do it.
value.literal: Using four to attack one, even if half deserted, we still had to do it.

value.zh: 是以不計死傷，與糧競也。
value.en: For this reason we did not count death and injury; we were racing against grain.
value.literal: For this reason we did not count death and injury; we were racing against grain.

value.zh: 今賊眾我寡，賊飢我飽，水雨乃爾，功力不設，雖當促之，亦何所為。
value.en: Now the enemy is many and we are few; the enemy is hungry and we are full. With rain and water like this, works cannot be set up. Even if we should hurry him, what would it accomplish?
value.literal: Now the enemy is many and we are few; the enemy is hungry and we are full. With rain and water like this, works cannot be set up. Even if we should hurry him, what would it accomplish?

value.zh: 自發京師，不憂賊攻，但恐賊走。
value.en: Since leaving the capital, I have not worried that the enemy would attack; I only feared that the enemy would flee.
value.literal: Since leaving the capital, I have not worried that the enemy would attack; I only feared that the enemy would flee.

value.zh: 今賊糧垂盡，而圍落未合，掠其牛馬，抄其樵采，此故驅之走也。
value.en: Now the enemy's grain is nearly exhausted, but the encirclement is not complete. To seize his cattle and horses and raid his woodcutters and gatherers would deliberately drive him to flee.
value.literal: Now the enemy's grain is nearly exhausted, but the encirclement is not complete. To seize his cattle and horses and raid his woodcutters and gatherers would deliberately drive him to flee.

value.zh: 夫兵者詭道，善因事變。
value.en: War is the way of deception, and the skillful respond to changes in affairs.
value.literal: War is the way of deception, and the skillful respond to changes in affairs.

value.zh: 賊憑眾恃雨，故雖飢困，未肯束手，當示無能以安之。
value.en: The enemy relies on numbers and trusts to the rain; therefore, though hungry and distressed, he is not yet willing to bind his hands. We should show inability in order to reassure him.
value.literal: The enemy relies on numbers and trusts to the rain; therefore, though hungry and distressed, he is not yet willing to bind his hands. We should show inability in order to reassure him.

value.zh: 取小利以驚之。
value.en: To take small advantages and alarm him
value.literal: To take small advantages and alarm him

value.zh: 非計也。」
value.en: is not a plan."
value.literal: is not a plan."

value.zh: 朝廷聞師遇雨，咸請召還。
value.en: Luoyang heard mud and demanded withdrawal.
value.literal: The court heard the army met rain and all petitioned recall.

value.zh: 天子曰：「司馬公臨危制變，計日擒之矣。」
value.en: The Son of Heaven said, "Sima Gong controls change in the face of danger; he will capture him on the calculated day."
value.literal: The Son of Heaven said, "Sima Gong controls change in the face of danger; he will capture him on the calculated day."

value.zh: 既而雨止，遂合圍。
value.en: Skies cleared; the ring closed.
value.literal: Soon the rain stopped and they completed the cordon.

value.zh: 起土山地道，楯櫓鉤橦，發矢石雨下，晝夜攻之。
value.en: They stacked siege mounds, bored mines, and hailed stone until the walls shook.
value.literal: They piled earth hills and dug tunnels—shields, rams, hooks—arrows and stones rained in assault day and night.

value.zh: 時有長星，色白，有芒鬣，自襄平城西南流于東北，墜於梁水，城中震慴。
value.en: A white comet streaked from Xiangping’s southwest to the Liang—terror seized the town.
value.literal: At that time a long comet appeared, white with bristling rays, flowing from southwest of Xiangping toward northeast, falling into the Liang River—the city shook with terror.

value.zh: 文懿大懼，乃使其所署相國王建、御史大夫柳甫乞降，請解圍面縛。
value.en: Yuan sent Wang Jian and Liu Fu pleading for the siege to lift so he could come out with bound hands.
value.literal: Wenyi was terrified and sent his appointed Chancellor Wang Jian and Imperial Counselor Liu Fu to beg surrender, asking to lift the siege so he could bind himself.

value.zh: 不許，執建等，皆斬之。
value.en: Sima Yi refused—seized the envoys and took their heads.
value.literal: He did not consent—seized Jian and the others and executed them all.

value.zh: 檄告文懿曰：「昔楚鄭列國，而鄭伯猶肉袒牽羊而迎之。
value.en: A proclamation informed Wenyì, saying, "In the past, Chu and Zheng were ranked states, yet the Earl of Zheng still bared his flesh, led a sheep, and went out to meet Chu.
value.literal: A proclamation informed Wenyì, saying, "In the past, Chu and Zheng were ranked states, yet the Earl of Zheng still bared his flesh, led a sheep, and went out to meet Chu.

value.zh: 孤為王人，位則上公，而建等欲孤解圍退舍，豈楚鄭之謂邪！
value.en: I am a man of the king, and my rank is that of an upper duke, yet Jian and the others wanted me to lift the siege and withdraw. Is this what was meant by Chu and Zheng?
value.literal: I am a man of the king, and my rank is that of an upper duke, yet Jian and the others wanted me to lift the siege and withdraw. Is this what was meant by Chu and Zheng?

value.zh: 二人老耄，必傳言失旨，已相為斬之。
value.en: The two men were old and confused and must have transmitted words contrary to their intent, so I have beheaded them for you.
value.literal: The two men were old and confused and must have transmitted words contrary to their intent, so I have beheaded them for you.

value.zh: 若意有未已，可更遣年少有明決者來。」
value.en: If your intention is not yet exhausted, you may send another younger man with clarity and resolution."
value.literal: If your intention is not yet exhausted, you may send another younger man with clarity and resolution."

value.zh: 文懿復遣侍中衞演乞剋日送任。
value.en: Yuan tried again—Wei Yan begging a hostage deadline.
value.literal: Wenyi again sent attendant Wei Yan requesting a fixed day to deliver hostages.

value.zh: 帝謂演曰：「軍事大要有五，能戰當戰，不能戰當守，不能守當走，餘二事惟有降與死耳。
value.en: The emperor told Yan, "There are five essentials in military affairs: if one can fight, one should fight; if one cannot fight, one should defend; if one cannot defend, one should flee. The remaining two matters are only surrender and death.
value.literal: The emperor told Yan, "There are five essentials in military affairs: if one can fight, one should fight; if one cannot fight, one should defend; if one cannot defend, one should flee. The remaining two matters are only surrender and death.

value.zh: 汝不肯面縛，此為決就死也，不須送任。」
value.en: You are unwilling to bind yourself face-forward; this means you have decided to go to death. There is no need to send hostages."
value.literal: You are unwilling to bind yourself face-forward; this means you have decided to go to death. There is no need to send hostages."

value.zh: 文懿攻南圍突出，帝縱兵擊敗之，斬于梁水之上星墜之所。
value.en: Yuan rammed the southern sector; Sima Yi crushed him and struck off his head where the comet had plunged.
value.literal: Wenyi assaulted the southern siege line trying to break out; the Emperor unleashed troops, defeated him, and beheaded him at the spot where the star fell above the Liang River.

value.zh: 既入城，立兩標以別新舊焉。
value.en: Inside the walls twin posts marked who belonged to the revolt.
value.literal: After entering the city he erected two markers to separate new guilt from old inhabitants.

value.zh: 男子年十五已上七千餘人皆殺之，以為京觀。
value.en: Seven thousand males above fifteen died for the victory mound.
value.literal: All males fifteen sui and older—more than seven thousand—were executed to form a burial mound.

value.zh: 偽公卿已下皆伏誅，戮其將軍畢盛等二千餘人。
value.en: Phony ministers died with two thousand officers including Bi Sheng.
value.literal: All false dukes and ministers downward were executed; more than two thousand including general Bi Sheng were put to death.

value.zh: 收戶四萬，口三十餘萬。
value.en: Registers captured forty thousand households and three hundred thousand people.
value.literal: Households registered numbered forty thousand; mouths exceeded three hundred thousand.

value.zh: 初，文懿篡其叔父恭位而囚之。
value.en: Yuan had seized Uncle Gong’s seat and jailed him.
value.literal: Earlier Wenyi had usurped his uncle Gong’s position and imprisoned him.

value.zh: 及將反，將軍綸直、賈範等苦諫，文懿皆殺之。
value.en: On the eve of revolt Lun Zhi and Jia Fan pleaded—Yuan murdered them.
value.literal: When about to rebel generals Lun Zhi and Jia Fan remonstrated bitterly—Wenyi executed them all.

value.zh: 帝乃釋恭之囚，封直等之墓，顯其遺嗣。
value.en: Sima Yi freed Gong, rebuilt martyrs’ graves, and ennobled their sons.
value.literal: The Emperor then released Gong from prison, tended the tombs of Zhi and others, and honored their surviving heirs.

value.zh: 令曰：「古之伐國，誅其鯨鯢而已，諸為文懿所詿誤者，皆原之。
value.en: The order said, "In antiquity, when states were attacked, only their great criminals were executed. All those misled by Wenyì are pardoned.
value.literal: The order said, "In antiquity, when states were attacked, only their great criminals were executed. All those misled by Wenyì are pardoned.

value.zh: 中國人欲還舊鄉，恣聽之。」
value.en: If people from the Central States wish to return to their old villages, let them do so freely."
value.literal: If people from the Central States wish to return to their old villages, let them do so freely."

value.zh: 時有兵士寒凍，乞襦，帝弗之與。
value.en: Frozen troops begged quilts; he withheld them.
value.literal: At that time soldiers freezing in the cold begged for padded jackets; the Emperor did not grant them.

value.zh: 或曰：「幸多故襦，可以賜之。」
value.en: Someone said, "Fortunately there are many old padded jackets; they can be given to them."
value.literal: Someone said, "Fortunately there are many old padded jackets; they can be given to them."

value.zh: 帝曰：「襦者官物，人臣無私施也。」
value.en: The emperor said, "Padded jackets are government property; a minister may not dispense them privately."
value.literal: The emperor said, "Padded jackets are government property; a minister may not dispense them privately."

value.zh: 乃奏軍人年六十已上者罷遣千餘人，將吏從軍死亡者致喪還家。
value.en: He cashiered thousand greybeards and shipped coffins west.
value.literal: He then memorialized to discharge over a thousand soldiers aged sixty and above and to send home the remains of officers who died on campaign.

value.zh: 遂班師。
value.en: Then he marched home.
value.literal: Thereupon he withdrew the army.

value.zh: 天子遣使者勞軍于薊，增封食昆陽，并前二縣。
value.en: Envoys met him at Ji with fresh fiefs—Kunyang added to two older counties.
value.literal: The Son of Heaven dispatched envoys to reward the army at Ji, enlarged the grain income with Kunyang, together with the previous two counties.

value.zh: 初，帝至襄平，夢天子枕其膝，曰：「視吾面。」
value.en: Earlier, when the emperor reached Xiangping, he dreamed that the Son of Heaven rested his head on his knees and said, "Look at my face."
value.literal: Earlier, when the emperor reached Xiangping, he dreamed that the Son of Heaven rested his head on his knees and said, "Look at my face."

value.zh: 俛視有異於常，心惡之。
value.en: Stooping to look, it differed from the ordinary, and his heart abhorred it.
value.literal: Stooping to look it differed from the ordinary—his heart reviled it.

value.zh: 先是，詔帝便道鎮關中；
value.en: Orders already told him to guard Guanzhong by detour.
value.literal: Earlier an edict had ordered the Emperor by convenient route to hold Guanzhong;

value.zh: 及次白屋，有詔召帝，三日之間，詔書五至。
value.en: At Baiwu five summons arrived in three days.
value.literal: When halting at Baiwu edicts summoned the Emperor—within three days five edicts arrived.

value.zh: 手詔曰：「間側息望到，到便直排閤入，視吾面。」
value.en: The handwritten edict said, "I am lying on my side, breath held, hoping you arrive. When you arrive, push straight through the doors and enter; look at my face."
value.literal: The handwritten edict said, "I am lying on my side, breath held, hoping you arrive. When you arrive, push straight through the doors and enter; look at my face."

value.zh: 帝大遽，乃乘追鋒車晝夜兼行，自白屋四百餘里，一宿而至。
value.en: Panic drove the relay carriage four hundred li overnight.
value.literal: The Emperor was greatly alarmed and rode the pursuit-chariot day and night—more than four hundred li from Baiwu, arriving in one night.

value.zh: 引入嘉福殿臥內，升御牀。
value.en: He was led into the inner chamber of Jiafu Hall and helped onto the imperial couch.
value.literal: He was conducted into the Jiafu Palace inner chamber and helped onto the imperial couch.

value.zh: 帝流涕問疾，天子執帝手，目齊王曰：「以後事相託。
value.en: The emperor wept and asked about his illness. The Son of Heaven took the emperor's hand, looked at the Prince of Qi, and said, "I entrust later affairs to you.
value.literal: The emperor wept and asked about his illness. The Son of Heaven took the emperor's hand, looked at the Prince of Qi, and said, "I entrust later affairs to you.

value.zh: 死乃復可忍，吾忍死待君，得相見，無所復恨矣。」
value.en: Only now can I bear to die. I endured death waiting for you; having seen you, I have no further regret."
value.literal: Only now can I bear to die. I endured death waiting for you; having seen you, I have no further regret."

value.zh: 與大將軍曹爽並受遺詔輔少主。
value.en: He and Cao Shuang sealed regency for the boy emperor.
value.literal: Together with Grand General Cao Shuang he received testamentary edicts to aid the young lord.

value.zh: 及齊王即帝位，遷侍中、持節、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，與爽各統兵三千人，共執朝政，更直殿中，乘輿入殿。
value.en: When the Prince of Qi ascended the throne, Sima Yi was promoted to palace attendant, bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of all armies inside and outside the capital, and recorder of affairs of the Secretariat. He and Shuang each commanded three thousand troops, jointly held court government, took turns on duty in the palace, and entered the palace by carriage.
value.literal: When the Prince of Qi ascended the throne, Sima Yi was promoted to palace attendant, bearer of the staff of authority, commander-in-chief of all armies inside and outside the capital, and recorder of affairs of the Secretariat. He and Shuang each commanded three thousand troops, jointly held court government, took turns on duty in the palace, and entered the palace by carriage.

value.zh: 爽欲使尚書奏事先由己，乃言於天子，徙帝為大司馬。
value.en: Shuang wanted memorials from the Secretariat to pass through him first, and therefore spoke to the Son of Heaven and transferred the emperor to be grand marshal.
value.literal: Shuang wanted memorials from the Secretariat to pass through him first, and therefore spoke to the Son of Heaven and transferred the emperor to be grand marshal.

value.zh: 朝議以為前後大司馬累薨於位，乃以帝為太傅，入殿不趨，贊拜不名，劍履上殿，如漢蕭何故事。
value.en: Court discussion held that former grand marshals had repeatedly died in office, and so the emperor was made grand tutor instead. He entered the palace hall without hurrying, was announced in audiences without being named, and went up into the hall with sword and shoes, following the precedent of Xiao He of Han.
value.literal: Court discussion held that former grand marshals had repeatedly died in office, and so the emperor was made grand tutor instead. He entered the palace hall without hurrying, was announced in audiences without being named, and went up into the hall with sword and shoes, following the precedent of Xiao He of Han.

value.zh: 嫁娶喪葬取給於官，以世子師為散騎常侍，子弟三人為列侯，四人為騎都尉。
value.en: Marriage and funeral expenses were supplied by the government; his heir Shi was made palace attendant cavalier, three sons and younger kinsmen were made listed marquises, and four were made cavalry commandants.
value.literal: Marriage and funeral expenses were supplied by the government; his heir Shi was made palace attendant cavalier, three sons and younger kinsmen were made listed marquises, and four were made cavalry commandants.

value.zh: 帝固讓子弟官不受。
value.en: The emperor firmly declined the offices for his sons and younger kinsmen and did not accept them.
value.literal: The emperor firmly declined the offices for his sons and younger kinsmen and did not accept them.

value.zh: 正始元年春正月，東倭重譯納貢，焉耆、危須諸國，弱水以南，鮮卑名王，皆遣使來獻。
value.en: In spring, the first month of the first year of Zhengshi (240), Eastern Wa sent tribute through multiple interpreters; Yanqi, Weixu, the states south of Ruoshui, and Xianbei titled kings all sent envoys to present offerings.
value.literal: In spring, the first month of the first year of Zhengshi (240), Eastern Wa sent tribute through multiple interpreters; Yanqi, Weixu, the states south of Ruoshui, and Xianbei titled kings all sent envoys to present offerings.

value.zh: 天子歸美宰輔，又增帝封邑。
value.en: The court credited the ministers and fattened Sima Yi’s lands.
value.literal: The Son of Heaven attributed glory to the chief ministers and again enlarged the Emperor’s fief.

value.zh: 初，魏明帝好修宮室，制度靡麗，百姓苦之。
value.en: Mingdi’s terraces had bled the people.
value.literal: Earlier Wei Mingdi loved constructing palaces—standards extravagant—the common people suffered.

value.zh: 帝自遼東還，役者猶萬餘人，雕玩之物動以千計。
value.en: Ten thousand corvée hands still carved gewgaws by the thousand.
value.literal: When the Emperor returned from Liaodong laborers still numbered over ten thousand; carved trinkets mounted by thousands.

value.zh: 至是皆奏罷之，節用務農，天下欣賴焉。
value.en: He stopped the yards, urged ploughs—the empire sighed relief.
value.literal: At this point all were memorialized to cease—economizing and promoting farming—the realm rejoiced and relied on him.

value.zh: 二年夏五月，吳將全琮寇芍陂，朱然、孫倫圍樊城，諸葛瑾、步騭掠柤中，帝請自討之。
value.en: Year two summer—Quan Zong hit Quebei, Zhu Ran and Sun Lun pinned Fan, Zhuge Jin and Bu Zhi ravaged Zhazhong—Sima Yi asked to ride south.
value.literal: Summer fifth month second year—Wu general Quan Zong raided Quebei; Zhu Ran and Sun Lun besieged Fancheng; Zhuge Jin and Bu Zhi raided Zhazhong—the Emperor requested to campaign himself.

value.zh: 議者咸言，賊遠來圍樊，不可卒拔。
value.en: Court wise men argued Wu sat far off—Fan would not fall fast.
value.literal: Discussants all said the rebels came from afar to besiege Fan—it cannot be quickly taken.

value.zh: 挫於堅城之下，有自破之勢，宜長策以御之。
value.en: Let prolonged defense drain them.
value.literal: Frustrated beneath stout walls they tend toward self-collapse—a long strategy should answer them.

value.zh: 帝曰：「邊城受敵而安坐廟堂，疆埸騷動，眾心疑惑，是社稷之大憂也。」
value.en: The emperor said, "For border cities to receive the enemy while we sit at ease in the court, with the frontier in turmoil and people's minds doubtful, is a great anxiety for the altars of soil and grain."
value.literal: The emperor said, "For border cities to receive the enemy while we sit at ease in the court, with the frontier in turmoil and people's minds doubtful, is a great anxiety for the altars of soil and grain."

value.zh: 六月，乃督諸軍南征，車駕送出津陽門。
value.en: Sixth month he took supreme command—throne carriage to Jinyang Gate.
value.literal: Sixth month—thereupon he commanded all armies south; imperial carriage escorted him out Jinyang Gate.

value.zh: 帝以南方暑溼，不宜持久，使輕騎挑之，然不敢動。
value.en: Humid south forbade long stays—light horse baited Zhu Ran; Ran stayed put.
value.literal: The Emperor considered the south hot and humid—not suited to long endurance—sent light cavalry to provoke them; Ran did not stir.

value.zh: 於是休戰士，簡精銳，募先登，申號令，示必攻之勢。
value.en: He rested men, culled shock troops, promised ladder gold, showed unstoppable assault.
value.literal: Thereupon he rested troops, picked elite, recruited first-assault climbers, proclaimed orders, displayed inevitable assault posture.

value.zh: 吳軍夜遁走，追至三州口，斬獲萬餘人，收其舟船軍資而還。
value.en: Wu fled by dark—Sanzhou Ford piled ten thousand heads and captured hulls.
value.literal: Wu army fled by night—pursued to Sanzhou kou, beheaded and captured over ten thousand, seized boats and military supplies and returned.

value.zh: 天子遣侍中常侍勞軍于宛。
value.en: The Son of Heaven dispatched a palace attendant and a regular attendant to reward the army at Wan.
value.literal: The Son of Heaven dispatched palace attendant and regular attendant to reward the army at Wan.

value.zh: 秋七月，增封食郾、臨潁，并前四縣，邑萬戶，子弟十一人皆為列侯。
value.en: That fall added Yan and Linying to four older counties—ten thousand taxable households—and eleven sons became column marquises.
value.literal: In autumn’s seventh month his income was enlarged with Yan and Linying; together with the previous four counties his households totaled ten thousand, and eleven sons were all enfeoffed as full marquises.

value.zh: 帝勳德日盛，而謙恭愈甚。
value.en: Honors mounted while he grew more deferential.
value.literal: The Emperor’s merit grew daily, yet his humility deepened.

value.zh: 以太常常林鄉邑舊齒，見之每拜。
value.en: He bowed to Chang Lin of the ministry whenever they crossed paths—hometown seniority demanded it.
value.literal: Because Minister of Ceremonies Chang Lin was an elder townsman, whenever they met the Emperor bowed.

value.zh: 恆戒子弟曰：「盛滿者道家之所忌，四時猶有推移，吾何德以堪之。
value.en: He constantly warned his sons and younger kinsmen, saying, "Fullness and excess are what the Daoist tradition avoids; even the four seasons still have alternation. What virtue do I have to bear this?
value.literal: He constantly warned his sons and younger kinsmen, saying, "Fullness and excess are what the Daoist tradition avoids; even the four seasons still have alternation. What virtue do I have to bear this?

value.zh: 損之又損之，庶可以免乎！」
value.en: Diminish it and diminish it again; perhaps then I can escape disaster!"
value.literal: Diminish it and diminish it again; perhaps then I can escape disaster!"

value.zh: 三年春，天子追封諡皇考京兆尹為舞陽成侯。
value.en: Spring of year three brought a posthumous marquisate on his father Fang.
value.literal: Third-year spring—the Son of Heaven posthumously titled his late father, Governor of Jingzhao, Marquis Cheng of Wuyang.

value.zh: 三月，奏穿廣漕渠，引河入汴，溉東南諸陂，始大佃於淮北。
value.en: He broke ground on the Guang canal, tapping the Yellow River into the Bian to flood Huai-north paddies.
value.literal: Third month—he memorialized to cut the Guang transport canal, divert the Yellow River into the Bian, irrigate the southeastern reservoirs, and begin large-scale farming north of the Huai.

value.zh: 先是，吳遣將諸葛恪屯皖，邊鄙苦之，帝欲自擊恪。
value.en: Zhuge Ke’s Wan garrison tormented the border—Sima Yi meant to lead the strike personally.
value.literal: Earlier Wu had stationed Zhuge Ke at Wan; the frontier suffered; the Emperor wished to attack Ke himself.

value.zh: 議者多以賊據堅城，積穀，欲引致官兵。
value.en: Critics said Wu baited Wei toward granary walls.
value.literal: Discussants mostly held that the rebels held a strong city and stored grain and wished to lure imperial troops.

value.zh: 今懸軍遠攻，其救必至，進退不易，未見其便。
value.en: A lone expedition invites rescue columns—movement becomes clumsy.
value.literal: Now an isolated army campaigns deep—relief must arrive; advance and retreat are awkward—the advantage is unclear.

value.zh: 帝曰：「賊之所長者水也，今攻其城，以觀其變。
value.en: The emperor said, "What the enemy excels in is water. Now we will attack his city, in order to observe his response.
value.literal: The emperor said, "What the enemy excels in is water. Now we will attack his city, in order to observe his response.

value.zh: 若用其所長，棄城奔走，此為廟勝也。
value.en: If he uses what he excels in and abandons the city to flee, this will be a victory in the temple calculations.
value.literal: If he uses what he excels in and abandons the city to flee, this will be a victory in the temple calculations.

value.zh: 若敢固守，湖水冬淺，船不得行，勢必棄水相救，由其所短，亦吾利也。」
value.en: If he dares to hold firm, lake water is shallow in winter and boats cannot move; circumstances will force him to abandon water and come to the rescue, and by his weakness this will also be to my advantage."
value.literal: If he dares to hold firm, lake water is shallow in winter and boats cannot move; circumstances will force him to abandon water and come to the rescue, and by his weakness this will also be to my advantage."

value.zh: 四年秋九月，帝督諸軍擊諸葛恪，車駕送出津陽門。
value.en: Autumn, ninth month, year four: full command against Zhuge Ke—throne carriage to Jinyang Gate.
value.literal: Fourth year, autumn ninth month—the Emperor commanded all armies against Zhuge Ke; the imperial carriage escorted him out the Jinyang Gate.

value.zh: 軍次於舒，恪焚燒積聚，棄城而遁。
value.en: The army halted at Shu; Ke burned his stores, abandoned the city, and fled.
value.literal: The army halted at Shu; Ke burned his stores, abandoned the city, and fled.

value.zh: 帝以滅賊之要，在於積穀，乃大興屯守，廣開淮陽、百尺二渠，又修諸陂於潁之南北，萬餘頃。
value.en: He bankrolled victory with dirt—Huaiyang and Baichi cuts, Ying basin dikes, ten thousand qing wet.
value.literal: The Emperor held that destroying rebels hinged on grain—therefore he massively expanded garrison farms, widened the Huaiyang and Baichi canals, and repaired reservoirs north and south of the Ying—more than ten thousand qing.

value.zh: [8]自是淮北倉庾相望，壽陽至於京師，[9]農官屯兵連屬焉。
value.en: [8] From then on granaries lined the region north of the Huai; [9] from Shouyang to the capital, agricultural officials and colony troops were linked.
value.literal: [8] From then on granaries lined the Huai north; [9] from Shouyang to the capital agricultural colonies and camps chained together.

value.zh: 五年春正月，帝至自淮南，天子使持節勞軍。
value.en: In the first month of spring of the fifth year the Emperor returned from Huainan; the Son of Heaven sent an envoy bearing the staff of authority to reward the army.
value.literal: First month of spring in the fifth year—the Emperor returned from Huainan; the Son of Heaven sent an envoy with insignia to reward the army.

value.zh: 尚書鄧颺、李勝等欲令曹爽建立功名，勸使伐蜀。
value.en: Deng Yang and Li Sheng pushed Shuang toward a Shu raid for glory.
value.literal: Ministers Deng Yang and Li Sheng wished Cao Shuang to earn merit and urged him to attack Shu.

value.zh: 帝止之，不可，爽果無功而還。
value.en: Sima Yi blocked it—Shuang marched anyway and limped home empty.
value.literal: The Emperor stopped him—without success—Shuang indeed returned without achievement.

value.zh: 六年秋八月，曹爽毀中壘中堅營，以兵屬其弟中領軍羲。
value.en: Autumn eight, year six: Shuang stripped the inner ramparts and handed steel to brother Xi.
value.literal: Sixth year, autumn eighth month—Cao Shuang dismantled the central bastion’s core camp and transferred troops to his younger brother Xi, Captain of the Central Army.

value.zh: 帝以先帝舊制禁之，不可。
value.en: He cited Mingdi’s bans—Shuang shrugged.
value.literal: The Emperor cited late emperor regulations forbidding this—it was not accepted.

value.zh: 冬十二月，天子詔帝朝會乘輿升殿。
value.en: Winter: Sima Yi earned carriage access to the throne hall.
value.literal: Winter twelfth month—the Son of Heaven issued an edict that at court assemblies the Emperor might ride the carriage onto the hall.

value.zh: 七年春正月，吳寇柤中，夷夏萬餘家避寇北渡沔。
value.en: Spring seven: Wu smashed Zhazhong—ten thousand families splashed north over the Han.
value.literal: Seventh year spring first month—Wu raided Zhazhong; Yi and Han households north of ten thousand fled the bandits across the Han.

value.zh: 帝以沔南近賊，若百姓奔還，必復致寇，宜權留之。
value.en: He argued refugees must stay north—returning invited another plunge.
value.literal: The Emperor held that south of the Han lay close to the foe—if commoners rushed back they would invite raid again—it was fitting temporarily to detain them.

value.zh: 曹爽曰：「今不能修守沔南而留百姓，非長策也。」
value.en: Cao Shuang said, "Now, if we cannot repair and defend south of the Mian yet leave the people there, it is not a long-term plan."
value.literal: Cao Shuang said, "Now, if we cannot repair and defend south of the Mian yet leave the people there, it is not a long-term plan."

value.zh: 帝曰：「不然。
value.en: The emperor said, "It is not so.
value.literal: The emperor said, "It is not so.

value.zh: 凡物致之安地則安，危地則危。
value.en: In general, when things are placed on secure ground, they are secure; when they are placed on dangerous ground, they are endangered.
value.literal: In general, when things are placed on secure ground, they are secure; when they are placed on dangerous ground, they are endangered.

value.zh: 故兵書曰『成敗，形也；
value.en: Therefore the military books say, 'Success and failure are a matter of form;
value.literal: Therefore the military books say, 'Success and failure are a matter of form;

value.zh: 安危，勢也』。
value.en: security and danger are a matter of configuration.'
value.literal: security and danger are a matter of configuration.'

value.zh: 形勢，御眾之要，不可以不審。
value.en: Form and configuration are essentials in controlling the masses and cannot fail to be examined carefully.
value.literal: Form and configuration are essentials in controlling the masses and cannot fail to be examined carefully.

value.zh: 設令賊以二萬人斷沔水，三萬人與沔南諸軍相持，萬人陸梁柤中，將何以救之？」
value.en: Suppose the enemy used twenty thousand men to cut off the Mian River, thirty thousand men to hold our various armies south of the Mian, and ten thousand men to range freely through Zhazhong. How would you rescue them?"
value.literal: Suppose the enemy used twenty thousand men to cut off the Mian River, thirty thousand men to hold our various armies south of the Mian, and ten thousand men to range freely through Zhazhong. How would you rescue them?"

value.zh: 爽不從，卒令還南。
value.en: Shuang forced the migration south anyway.
value.literal: Shuang did not follow—ultimately ordered them returned south.

value.zh: 賊果襲破柤中，所失萬計。
value.en: Wu shattered Zhazhong—myriad gone.
value.literal: The bandits indeed struck and broke Zhazhong—losses numbered ten thousand.

value.zh: 八年夏四月，夫人張氏薨。
value.en: Eighth year summer: wife Zhang passed.
value.literal: Summer fourth month eighth year—Lady Zhang died.

value.zh: 曹爽用何晏、鄧颺、丁謐之謀，遷太后於永寧宮，專擅朝政，兄弟并典禁兵，多樹親黨，屢改制度。
value.en: Shuang locked the dowager away, stacked brothers on the guards, rewrote laws with He Yan’s cabal.
value.literal: Cao Shuang employed He Yan, Deng Yang, and Ding Mi’s plots—shifted the empress dowager to Yongning Palace, monopolized court governance, brothers jointly commanded palace guards, planted partisans widely, repeatedly altered institutions.

value.zh: 帝不能禁，於是與爽有隙。
value.en: Sima Yi could not brake him—rift opened.
value.literal: The Emperor could not restrain him—thereupon grew estranged from Shuang.

value.zh: 五月，帝稱疾不與政事。
value.en: He pleaded sick and vanished from council.
value.literal: Fifth month—the Emperor claimed illness and withdrew from governance.

value.zh: 時人為之謠曰：「何、鄧、丁，亂京城。」
value.en: People of the time made a song about them, saying, "He, Deng, and Ding throw the capital into disorder."
value.literal: People of the time made a song about them, saying, "He, Deng, and Ding throw the capital into disorder."

value.zh: 九年春三月，黃門張當私出掖庭才人石英等十一人，與曹爽為伎人。
value.en: Yellow Gate Zhang Dang secretly brought eleven palace talents including Shi Ying out of the inner court as entertainers for Cao Shuang.
value.literal: Spring third month ninth year—Yellow Gate Zhang Dang secretly brought eleven palace talents including Shi Ying out of the forbidden precincts as entertainers for Cao Shuang.

value.zh: 爽、晏謂帝疾篤，遂有無君之心，與當密謀，圖危社稷，期有日矣。
value.en: They thought Sima Yi dying and schemed usurpation with Zhang Dang.
value.literal: Shuang and Yan deemed the Emperor mortally ill—thereupon harbored disloyal intent—plotting secretly with Dang to endanger the altars—a date was set.

value.zh: 帝亦潛為之備，爽之徒屬亦頗疑帝。
value.en: Sima Yi armed in shadows while Shuang’s men sniffed trap.
value.literal: The Emperor also secretly prepared; Shuang’s followers likewise suspected the Emperor.

value.zh: 會河南尹李勝將莅荊州，來候帝。
value.en: When the Governor of Henan, Li Sheng, was about to take up Jingzhou, he came to visit the emperor.
value.literal: When Governor of Henan Li Sheng was about to take up Jingzhou he came to visit the Emperor.

value.zh: 帝詐疾篤，使兩婢侍，持衣衣落，指口言渴，婢進粥，帝不持杯飲，粥皆流出霑胸。
value.en: He staged palsy—maids, spilled porridge, sodden robes.
value.literal: The Emperor feigned grave illness—had two maids attend—when dressing let clothes fall—pointed to mouth saying thirst—maids brought gruel—the Emperor could not hold cup—gruel spilled soaking chest.

value.zh: 勝曰：「眾情謂明公舊風發動，何意尊體乃爾！」
value.en: Sheng said, "Everyone thought Your Lordship's old wind illness had acted up. How could your honored body be like this!"
value.literal: Sheng said, "Everyone thought Your Lordship's old wind illness had acted up. How could your honored body be like this!"

value.zh: 帝使聲氣纔屬，說「年老枕疾，死在旦夕。
value.en: The emperor made his voice and breath barely connect and said, "I am old and bedridden with illness; death is at morning or evening.
value.literal: The emperor made his voice and breath barely connect and said, "I am old and bedridden with illness; death is at morning or evening.

value.zh: 君當屈并州，并州近胡，善為之備。
value.en: You are going to serve in Bingzhou. Bingzhou is close to the Hu; prepare well for it.
value.literal: You are going to serve in Bingzhou. Bingzhou is close to the Hu; prepare well for it.

value.zh: 恐不復相見，以子師、昭兄弟為託」。
value.en: I fear we will not see each other again, so I entrust my sons Shi and Zhao, the brothers, to you."
value.literal: I fear we will not see each other again, so I entrust my sons Shi and Zhao, the brothers, to you."

value.zh: 勝曰：「當還忝本州，非并州。」
value.en: Sheng said, "I am returning to serve in my home province, not Bingzhou."
value.literal: Sheng said, "I am returning to serve in my home province, not Bingzhou."

value.zh: 帝乃錯亂其辭曰：「君方到并州。」
value.en: The emperor then deliberately confused his words and said, "You are just going to Bingzhou."
value.literal: The emperor then deliberately confused his words and said, "You are just going to Bingzhou."

value.zh: 勝復曰：「當忝荊州。」
value.en: Sheng again said, "I am going to serve in Jingzhou."
value.literal: Sheng again said, "I am going to serve in Jingzhou."

value.zh: 帝曰：「年老意荒，不解君言。
value.en: The emperor said, "In old age my mind is confused, and I did not understand your words.
value.literal: The emperor said, "In old age my mind is confused, and I did not understand your words.

value.zh: 今還為本州，盛德壯烈，好建功勳！」
value.en: Now you are returning to your home province; with flourishing virtue and vigorous valor, build fine achievements!"
value.literal: Now you are returning to your home province; with flourishing virtue and vigorous valor, build fine achievements!"

value.zh: 勝退告爽曰：「司馬公尸居餘氣，形神已離，不足慮矣。」
value.en: After Sheng withdrew, he told Shuang, "Sima Gong lies like a corpse with only remnant breath; his form and spirit have already separated. He is not worth worrying about."
value.literal: After Sheng withdrew, he told Shuang, "Sima Gong lies like a corpse with only remnant breath; his form and spirit have already separated. He is not worth worrying about."

value.zh: 他日，又言曰：「太傅不可復濟，令人愴然。」
value.en: Another day, he also said, "The Grand Tutor can no longer be saved; it makes one grieve."
value.literal: Another day, he also said, "The Grand Tutor can no longer be saved; it makes one grieve."

value.zh: 故爽等不復設備。
value.en: Shuang stood down his guard.
value.literal: Therefore Shuang and others ceased preparing defenses.

value.zh: 嘉平元年春正月甲午，天子謁高平陵，爽兄弟皆從。
value.en: In spring, the first month, jiawu, of the first year of Jiaping (249), the Son of Heaven paid respects at Gaoping Mausoleum, and Shuang and his brothers all accompanied him.
value.literal: In spring, the first month, jiawu, of the first year of Jiaping (249), the Son of Heaven paid respects at Gaoping Mausoleum, and Shuang and his brothers all accompanied him.

value.zh: 是日，太白襲月。
value.en: Metal star gnawed the moon that dawn.
value.literal: That day Venus occulted the moon.

value.zh: 帝于是奏永寧太后廢爽兄弟。
value.en: Empress warrant arrived—strip Shuang brothers.
value.literal: The Emperor thereupon memorialized Empress Dowager Yongning to depose Shuang brothers.

value.zh: 時景帝為中護軍，將兵屯司馬門。
value.en: Sima Shi held Sima Gate.
value.literal: At that time Emperor Jing served as Colonel Protecting the Army—commanded troops camped at Sima Gate.

value.zh: 帝列陣闕下，經爽門。
value.en: Sima Yi formed ranks below Duan—passed Shuang mansion.
value.literal: The Emperor drew battle lines below the palace gate—passed Shuang’s gate.

value.zh: 爽帳下督嚴世上樓，引弩將射帝，孫謙止之曰：「事未可知。」
value.en: Yan Shi, a commander under Shuang, went up the tower and drew a crossbow to shoot the emperor, but Sun Qian stopped him, saying, "The matter cannot yet be known."
value.literal: Yan Shi, a commander under Shuang, went up the tower and drew a crossbow to shoot the emperor, but Sun Qian stopped him, saying, "The matter cannot yet be known."

value.zh: 三注三止，皆引其肘不得發。
value.en: Three drawn bolts—three stays—never fired.
value.literal: Three times he drew—three times stopped—all pulling his elbow unable to loose.

value.zh: 大司農桓範出赴爽，蔣濟言於帝曰：「智囊往矣。」
value.en: When Grand Minister of Agriculture Huan Fan left to join Shuang, Jiang Ji said to the emperor, "The wisdom bag has gone."
value.literal: When Grand Minister of Agriculture Huan Fan left to join Shuang, Jiang Ji said to the emperor, "The wisdom bag has gone."

value.zh: 帝曰：「爽與範內疏而智不及，駑馬戀短豆，必不能用也。」
value.en: The emperor said, "Shuang and Fan are inwardly estranged, and his wisdom is not equal to Fan's. A worn-out horse longs for short beans; he certainly will not use him."
value.literal: The emperor said, "Shuang and Fan are inwardly estranged, and his wisdom is not equal to Fan's. A worn-out horse longs for short beans; he certainly will not use him."

value.zh: 於是假司徒高柔節，行大將軍事，領爽營，謂柔曰：「君為周勃矣。」
value.en: Thereupon he borrowed Situ Gao Rou's staff, made him acting general-in-chief, put him in command of Shuang's camp, and said to Rou, "You are Zhou Bo."
value.literal: Thereupon he borrowed Situ Gao Rou's staff, made him acting general-in-chief, put him in command of Shuang's camp, and said to Rou, "You are Zhou Bo."

value.zh: 命太僕王觀行中領軍，攝羲營。
value.en: Wang Guan seized Xi’s guards.
