value.literal: He ordered Minister Coachman Wang Guan to act as Central Army colonel—take Xi’s camp.

value.zh: 帝親帥太尉蔣濟等勒兵出迎天子，屯于洛水浮橋，上奏曰：「先帝詔陛下、秦王及臣升於御牀，握臣臂曰『深以後事為念』。
value.en: The emperor personally led Grand Commandant Jiang Ji and others, drew up troops, went out to meet the Son of Heaven, encamped at the floating bridge over the Luo River, and memorialized, "The late emperor ordered Your Majesty, the Prince of Qin, and me to ascend the imperial couch, grasped my arm, and said, 'I am deeply mindful of later affairs.'
value.literal: The emperor personally led Grand Commandant Jiang Ji and others, drew up troops, went out to meet the Son of Heaven, encamped at the floating bridge over the Luo River, and memorialized, "The late emperor ordered Your Majesty, the Prince of Qin, and me to ascend the imperial couch, grasped my arm, and said, 'I am deeply mindful of later affairs.'

value.zh: 今大將軍爽背棄顧命，敗亂國典，內則僭擬，外專威權。
value.en: Now General-in-Chief Shuang has turned his back on the charge left to him, thrown the institutions of the state into disorder, usurps forms within, and monopolizes authority without.
value.literal: Now General-in-Chief Shuang has turned his back on the charge left to him, thrown the institutions of the state into disorder, usurps forms within, and monopolizes authority without.

value.zh: 羣官要職，皆置所親；
value.en: For the important offices among the assembled officials, he has installed only those close to him;
value.literal: For the important offices among the assembled officials, he has installed only those close to him;

value.zh: 宿衞舊人，並見斥黜。
value.en: the old members of the palace guard have all been rejected and dismissed.
value.literal: the old members of the palace guard have all been rejected and dismissed.

value.zh: 根據槃互，縱恣日甚。
value.en: His roots and bases intertwine, and his arrogance grows worse by the day.
value.literal: His roots and bases intertwine, and his arrogance grows worse by the day.

value.zh: 又以黃門張當為都監，專共交關，伺候神器。
value.en: He has also made the Yellow Gates officer Zhang Dang metropolitan inspector, and they alone exchange connections and watch for the divine vessel.
value.literal: He has also made the Yellow Gates officer Zhang Dang metropolitan inspector, and they alone exchange connections and watch for the divine vessel.

value.zh: 天下洶洶，人懷危懼。
value.en: All under Heaven is in turmoil, and people harbor danger and fear.
value.literal: All under Heaven is in turmoil, and people harbor danger and fear.

value.zh: 陛下便為寄坐，豈得久安？
value.en: Your Majesty has thereby become one seated in dependency; how can you long be secure?
value.literal: Your Majesty has thereby become one seated in dependency; how can you long be secure?

value.zh: 此非先帝詔陛下及臣升御牀之本意也。
value.en: This was not the original intent of the late emperor when he ordered Your Majesty and me to ascend the imperial couch.
value.literal: This was not the original intent of the late emperor when he ordered Your Majesty and me to ascend the imperial couch.

value.zh: 臣雖朽邁，敢忘前言。
value.en: Though I am decayed and old, how would I dare forget the former words?
value.literal: Though I am decayed and old, how would I dare forget the former words?

value.zh: 昔趙高極意，秦是以亡；
value.en: In the past, Zhao Gao fulfilled his will to the utmost, and Qin thereby perished;
value.literal: In the past, Zhao Gao fulfilled his will to the utmost, and Qin thereby perished;

value.zh: 呂霍早斷，漢祚永延。
value.en: the Lu and Huo clans were cut off early, and the Han mandate was prolonged forever.
value.literal: the Lu and Huo clans were cut off early, and the Han mandate was prolonged forever.

value.zh: 此乃陛下之殷鑒，臣授命之秋也。
value.en: This is Your Majesty's clear warning and the moment when I receive my command.
value.literal: This is Your Majesty's clear warning and the moment when I receive my command.

value.zh: 公卿羣臣皆以爽有無君之心，兄弟不宜典兵宿衞；
value.en: The high ministers and assembled officials all consider Shuang to have a heart that recognizes no ruler, and that the brothers should not control troops and the palace guard;
value.literal: The high ministers and assembled officials all consider Shuang to have a heart that recognizes no ruler, and that the brothers should not control troops and the palace guard;

value.zh: 奏皇太后，皇太后敕如奏施行。
value.en: they memorialized the Empress Dowager, and the Empress Dowager ordered that it be carried out as memorialized.
value.literal: they memorialized the Empress Dowager, and the Empress Dowager ordered that it be carried out as memorialized.

value.zh: 臣輒敕主者及黃門令罷爽、羲、訓吏兵，各以本官侯就第。
value.en: I have therefore ordered the responsible officials and the Director of the Yellow Gates to remove Shuang, Xi, and Xun from their officials and troops, and for each, as a marquis with his original office, to go to his residence.
value.literal: I have therefore ordered the responsible officials and the Director of the Yellow Gates to remove Shuang, Xi, and Xun from their officials and troops, and for each, as a marquis with his original office, to go to his residence.

value.zh: 若稽留車駕，以軍法從事。
value.en: If they delay the imperial carriage, handle them under military law.
value.literal: If they delay the imperial carriage, handle them under military law.

value.zh: 臣輒力疾將兵詣洛水浮橋，伺察非常。」
value.en: I have therefore forced myself through illness and led troops to the floating bridge over the Luo River, to watch for the extraordinary."
value.literal: I have therefore forced myself through illness and led troops to the floating bridge over the Luo River, to watch for the extraordinary."

value.zh: 爽不通奏，留車駕宿伊水南，伐樹為鹿角，發屯兵數千人以守。
value.en: Shuang did not transmit the memorial, detained the imperial carriage overnight south of the Yi River, felled trees for palisades, and called several thousand garrison troops to defend.
value.literal: Shuang did not transmit memorial—detained imperial carriage south of Yi River overnight—felled trees for antlers—called several thousand garrison troops to defend.

value.zh: 桓範果勸爽奉天子幸許昌，移檄徵天下兵。
value.en: Fan beg march to Xuchang—levy realm.
value.literal: Huan Fan indeed urged Shuang to escort Son of Heaven to Xuchang—issue proclamations summoning troops empire-wide.

value.zh: 爽不能用，而夜遣侍中許允、尚書陳泰詣帝，觀望風旨。
value.en: Shuang failed nerve—sent Xu Yun and Chen Tai to sniff terms.
value.literal: Shuang could not use this—by night sent Palace Attendant Xu Yun and Minister Chen Tai to the Emperor—probe intentions.

value.zh: 帝數其過失，事止免官。
value.en: Sima Yi listed crimes—offer stripped posts.
value.literal: The Emperor enumerated his faults—matter stopped at dismissal from office.

value.zh: 泰還以報爽，勸之通奏。
value.en: Chen Tai urged surrender memorial.
value.literal: Tai returned reporting to Shuang—urged transmitting memorial.

value.zh: 帝又遣爽所信殿中校尉尹大目諭爽，指洛水為誓，爽意信之。
value.en: Yin Damu swore on Luo—Shuang believed.
value.literal: The Emperor again sent Shuang’s trusted Palace Inspector Yin Damu to instruct Shuang—pointed to Luo River swearing oath—Shuang’s heart trusted.

value.zh: 桓範等援引古今，諫說萬端。
value.en: Fan pleaded classics till hoarse.
value.literal: Huan Fan and others cited ancient and modern—remonstrated myriad ways.

value.zh: 終不能從，乃曰：「司馬公正當欲奪吾權耳。
value.en: In the end Shuang could not follow Fan, and then said, "Sima Gong merely wants to seize my authority.
value.literal: In the end Shuang could not follow Fan, and then said, "Sima Gong merely wants to seize my authority.

value.zh: 吾得以侯還第，不失為富家翁。」
value.en: If I can return to my residence as a marquis, I will not fail to be a wealthy old gentleman."
value.literal: If I can return to my residence as a marquis, I will not fail to be a wealthy old gentleman."

value.zh: 範拊膺曰：「坐卿，滅吾族矣！」
value.en: Fan beat his breast and said, "Because of you, my clan will be destroyed!"
value.literal: Fan beat his breast and said, "Because of you, my clan will be destroyed!"

value.zh: 遂通帝奏。
value.en: Shuang folded—sent memorial.
value.literal: Thereupon transmitted Emperor memorial.

value.zh: 既而有司劾黃門張當，并發爽與何晏等反事，乃收爽兄弟及其黨與何晏、丁謐、鄧颺、畢軌、李勝、桓範等誅之。
value.en: Indictments landed—Zhang Dang flipped—Shuang ring executed wholesale.
value.literal: Soon judicial officials impeached Yellow Gate Zhang Dang—and uncovered Shuang with He Yan and others rebellion matter—thereupon seized Shuang brothers and faction He Yan, Ding Mi, Deng Yang, Bi Gui, Li Sheng, Huan Fan etc.—executed.

value.zh: 蔣濟曰：「曹真之勳，不可以不祀。」
value.en: Jiang Ji said, "Cao Zhen's merits cannot be left without sacrifice."
value.literal: Jiang Ji said, "Cao Zhen's merits cannot be left without sacrifice."

value.zh: 帝不聽。
value.en: Sima Yi refused.
value.literal: The Emperor did not listen.

value.zh: 初，爽司馬魯芝、主簿楊綜斬關奔爽。
value.en: Lu Zhi and Yang Zong had bolted to Shuang.
value.literal: Earlier Shuang’s marshal Lu Zhi and clerk Yang Zong broke passes fleeing to Shuang.

value.zh: 及爽之將歸罪也，芝、綜泣諫曰：「公居伊周之任，挾天子，杖天威，孰敢不從？
value.en: When Shuang was about to return and submit to punishment, Zhi and Zong wept and remonstrated, saying, "You occupy the office of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, hold the Son of Heaven, and rely on Heaven's authority. Who would dare not follow?
value.literal: When Shuang was about to return and submit to punishment, Zhi and Zong wept and remonstrated, saying, "You occupy the office of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, hold the Son of Heaven, and rely on Heaven's authority. Who would dare not follow?

value.zh: 舍此而欲就東市，豈不痛哉！」
value.en: To abandon this and want to go to the eastern market for execution, is it not painful!"
value.literal: To abandon this and want to go to the eastern market for execution, is it not painful!"

value.zh: 有司奏收芝、綜科罪，帝赦之，曰：「以勸事君者。」
value.en: The responsible offices memorialized to arrest Zhi and Zong and assign crimes, but the emperor pardoned them, saying, "To encourage those who serve their lords."
value.literal: The responsible offices memorialized to arrest Zhi and Zong and assign crimes, but the emperor pardoned them, saying, "To encourage those who serve their lords."

value.zh: 二月，天子以帝為丞相，增封潁川之繁昌、鄢陵、新汲、父城，并前八縣，邑二萬戶，奏事不名。
value.en: February: chancellor, four Yingchuan counties stacked on eight—twenty thousand households—name suppressed on memorials.
value.literal: Second month—the Son of Heaven made the Emperor Chancellor, enlarged his income with Fanchang, Yanling, Xinji, and Fucheng in Yingchuan—together eight counties previously—twenty thousand households—and memorialized without naming himself.

value.zh: 固讓丞相。
value.en: He refused the chancellor seal.
value.literal: He firmly declined Chancellor.

value.zh: 冬十二月，加九錫之禮，朝會不拜。
value.en: Winter: Nine tins—stood straight at audience.
value.literal: Winter twelfth month—the Nine Bestowals ritual was added—at court assemblies he did not bow.

value.zh: 固讓九錫。
value.en: He refused the nine insignia.
value.literal: He firmly declined the Nine Bestowals.

value.zh: 二年春正月，天子命帝立廟于洛陽，置左右長史，增掾屬、舍人滿十人，歲舉掾屬任御史、秀才各一人，增官騎百人，鼓吹十四人，封子肜平樂亭侯，倫安樂亭侯。
value.en: Spring year two: Luoyang ancestral shrine, full clerical staff, ten advisors, yearly recommendations, hundred escorts, fourteen pipes—sons Rong and Lun petty marquises.
value.literal: Second year spring first month—the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor to erect a temple in Luoyang, assign left and right senior clerks, enlarge aides and attendants to ten men fully, annually nominate one aide each for censor and xiucai, add one hundred official riders and fourteen musicians, enfeoff son Rong as marquis of Pingle ting and Lun as marquis of Anle ting.

value.zh: 帝以久疾不任朝請，每有大事，天子親幸第以諮訪焉。
value.en: Too ill for court—emperor rode to his gate for counsel.
value.literal: The Emperor because of long illness could not attend court audiences—whenever great affairs arose the Son of Heaven personally visited his mansion for consultation.

value.zh: 兗州刺史令狐愚、、太尉王淩貳於帝，謀立楚王彪。
value.en: The Inspector of Yanzhou, Linghu Yu, and Grand Commandant Wang Ling rebelled against the Emperor, plotting to install Prince Biao of Chu.
value.literal: Inspector of Yanzhou Linghu Yu [sic—duplicate punctuation in source] and Grand Commandant Wang Ling rebelled against the Emperor—plotting to install Prince Biao of Chu.

value.zh: 三年春正月，王淩詐言吳人塞涂水，請發兵以討之。
value.en: Year three spring: Wang Ling lied Wu jammed Tu ford—begged arms.
value.literal: Third year spring first month—Wang Ling falsely claimed Wu men blocked the Tu River—requested mobilizing troops to attack.

value.zh: 帝潛知其計，不聽。
value.en: Sima Yi saw through it—denied arms.
value.literal: The Emperor secretly knew his scheme—did not consent.

value.zh: 夏四月，帝自帥中軍，汎舟沿流，九日而到甘城。
value.en: Fourth month: central army by river—nine days to Gancheng.
value.literal: Summer fourth month—the Emperor personally led the central army—boated downstream—nine days reaching Gancheng.

value.zh: 淩計無所出，乃迎於武丘，面縛水次，曰：「淩若有罪，公當折簡召淩，何苦自來邪！」
value.en: With no plan available, Wang Ling went out to meet him at Wuqiu, bound himself before him at the riverside, and said, "If I had committed a crime, you should have summoned me with a folded note. Why trouble yourself to come in person!"
value.literal: With no plan available, Wang Ling went out to meet him at Wuqiu, bound himself before him at the riverside, and said, "If I had committed a crime, you should have summoned me with a folded note. Why trouble yourself to come in person!"

value.zh: 帝曰：「以君非折簡之客故耳。」
value.en: The emperor said, "It is only because you are not a guest for a folded note."
value.literal: The emperor said, "It is only because you are not a guest for a folded note."

value.zh: 即以淩歸于京師。
value.en: Thereupon he took Wang Ling back to the capital.
value.literal: Thereupon took Ling back toward capital.

value.zh: 道經賈逵廟，淩呼曰：「賈梁道！
value.en: As the road passed the shrine of Jia Kui, Wang Ling cried out, "Jia Liangdao!
value.literal: As the road passed the shrine of Jia Kui, Wang Ling cried out, "Jia Liangdao!

value.zh: 王淩是大魏之忠臣，惟爾有神知之。」
value.en: Wang Ling is a loyal minister of Great Wei; only you, if you have spirit, know it."
value.literal: Wang Ling is a loyal minister of Great Wei; only you, if you have spirit, know it."

value.zh: 至項，仰鴆而死。
value.en: At Xiang he swallowed poison.
value.literal: Arriving at Xiang drank poison and died.

value.zh: 收其餘黨，皆夷三族，并殺彪。
value.en: Purged networks—three kin wipes—and Prince Biao.
value.literal: Seized remainder faction—all extirpated three clans—and executed Biao.

value.zh: 悉錄魏諸王公置于鄴，命有司監察，不得交關。
value.en: Caged Wei royalty at Ye—wardens barred intrigue.
value.literal: Registered all Wei princes and dukes at Ye—ordered officials supervise—no conspiracy.

value.zh: 天子遣侍中韋誕持節勞軍于五池。
value.en: The Son of Heaven sent Palace Attendant Wei Dan with a staff of authority to reward the army at Wuchi.
value.literal: Son of Heaven dispatched Palace Attendant Wei Dan with insignia to reward army at Wuchi.

value.zh: 帝至自甘城，天子又使兼大鴻臚、太僕庾嶷持節，策命帝為相國，封安平郡公，孫及兄子各一人為列侯，前後食邑五萬戶，侯者十九人。
value.en: Second investiture: minister of state, Anping duke, nineteen marquis slots—fifty thousand households.
value.literal: The Emperor returned from Gancheng. The Son of Heaven again ordered Yu Yi, concurrent Grand Herald and Minister Coachman, with a staff of authority, to appoint the Emperor Minister of State and enfeoff him as Duke of Anping Commandery; one grandson and one elder brother’s son each as a column marquis; food-fiefs totaling fifty thousand households; nineteen marquises in all.

value.zh: 固讓相國、郡公不受。
value.en: Refused duke and minister posts.
value.literal: Firmly declined minister of state and commandery duke—did not accept.

value.zh: 六月，帝寢疾，夢賈逵、王淩為祟，甚惡之。
value.en: Summer sixth: nightmares of Jia Kui and Wang Ling.
value.literal: Sixth month—Emperor bedridden illness—dreamed Jia Kui and Wang Ling haunted him—greatly loathed.

value.zh: 秋八月戊寅，崩於京師，時年七十三。
value.en: Died Luoyang seventy-three.
value.literal: Autumn eighth month wuyin—perished at capital—aged seventy-three.

value.zh: 天子素服臨弔，喪葬威儀依漢霍光故事，追贈相國、郡公。
value.en: The emperor wore mourning and oversaw rites on the Huo Guang model—then piled minister of state and duke honors on the dead.
value.literal: The Son of Heaven wore unpatterned mourning dress and attended the obsequies—burial majesty followed Han Huo Guang precedent—and posthumously gifted minister of state and commandery duke.

value.zh: 弟孚表陳先志，辭郡公及轀輬車。
value.en: Sima Fu cited Sima Yi’s will—refusing ducal rank and the ornate burial cart.
value.literal: Younger brother Fu memorialized his late brother’s wishes—declining commandery duke rank and the imperial hearse.

value.zh: 九月庚申，葬于河陰，諡曰文，後改諡宣文。
value.en: Buried Heyin—first Wen then Xu Wen.
value.literal: Ninth month gengshen—buried Heyin—posthumous title Wen—later altered Xu Wen.

value.zh: 先是，預作終制，於首陽山為土藏，不墳不樹；
value.en: Pre-dug Shouyang grave—flat earth—no mound trees;
value.literal: Earlier prepared terminal instructions—earth tomb at Shouyang Mountain—no mound no trees;

value.zh: 作顧命三篇，斂以時服，不設明器，後終者不得合葬。
value.en: three wills—seasonal shroud—no mingqi—no later joint burial.
value.literal: composed testament three chapters—shroud in seasonal clothes—no grave goods—later deceased may not joint bury.

value.zh: 一如遺命。
value.en: Burial obeyed will.
value.literal: All accorded testament charge.

value.zh: 晉國初建，追尊曰宣王。
value.en: Jin raised him King Xuan.
value.literal: When Jin state first founded posthumously honored King Xuan.

value.zh: 武帝受禪，上尊號曰宣皇帝，陵曰高原，廟稱高祖。
value.en: When Emperor Wu accepted the abdication he raised the honorific Emperor Xuan; the mausoleum was Gaoyuan; the temple name was Gaozu.
value.literal: When Wu-di accepted abdication elevated honorific Emperor Xuan—mausoleum Gaoyuan—temple styled Gaozu.

value.zh: 帝內忌而外寬，猜忌多權變。
value.en: Inside jealous—outside mild—paranoia masked.
value.literal: The Emperor inwardly jealous outwardly generous—suspicious—many stratagems.

value.zh: 魏武察帝有雄豪志，聞有狼顧相，欲驗之。
value.en: Cao Cao tested wolf-turn rumor.
value.literal: Emperor Wu observed the Emperor bore heroic ambition—heard he had wolf-gaze physiognomy—wished to verify.

value.zh: 乃召使前行，令反顧，面正向後而身不動。
value.en: Ordered forward—snap neck—wolf stare.
value.literal: Summoned ordering advance march—commanded turn head—face squared rear yet body unmoved.

value.zh: 又嘗夢三馬同食一槽，甚惡焉。
value.en: Dreamed three horses one trough—dread.
value.literal: Also once dreamed three horses shared one trough—greatly loathed.

value.zh: 因謂太子丕曰：「司馬懿非人臣也，必預汝家事。」
value.en: He therefore said to Crown Prince Pi, "Sima Yi is no mere subject; he will certainly take part in your family affairs."
value.literal: He therefore said to Crown Prince Pi, "Sima Yi is no mere subject; he will certainly take part in your family affairs."

value.zh: 太子素與帝善，每相全佑，故免。
value.en: Pi shielded him—survived.
value.literal: Heir always friendly with Emperor—each time wholly protected—therefore spared.

value.zh: 帝於是勤於吏職，夜以忘寢，至於芻牧之間，悉皆臨履，由是魏武意遂安。
value.en: Burned ledgers nightly—Cao Cao relaxed.
value.literal: Thereupon Emperor diligent in clerical duties—night forgot sleep—even fodder matters personally inspected—thereby Emperor Wu’s mind settled.

value.zh: 及平公孫文懿，大行殺戮。
value.en: When he pacified Gongsun Wenyi he carried out a great slaughter.
value.literal: When pacifying Gongsun Wenyi greatly conducted slaughter.

value.zh: 誅曹爽之際，支黨皆夷及三族，男女無少長，姑姊妹女子之適人者皆殺之，既而竟遷魏鼎云。
value.en: Shuang purge erased kin—even married women—then stole Wei.
value.literal: When executing Cao Shuang faction all branches extirpated three clans—male female none spared young old—aunts sisters daughters married all killed—thereafter indeed shifted Wei tripod.

value.zh: 明帝時，王導侍坐。
value.en: Emperor Ming of Jin held Wang Dao beside him.
value.literal: During Emperor Ming’s reign Wang Dao attended seated.

value.zh: 帝問前世所以得天下，導乃陳帝創業之始，及文帝末高貴鄉公事。
value.en: Ming asked Jin’s rise—Wang Dao traced Sima Yi through Gaoguixiang coup.
value.literal: Emperor asked how former age gained realm—Dao therefore narrated Emperor’s founding beginnings and Wen emperor end affair of Duke Gaoguixiang.

value.zh: 明帝以面覆牀曰：「若如公言，晉祚復安得長遠！」
value.en: Emperor Ming covered his face against the bed and said, "If it is as you say, how could the Jin mandate again be long-lasting!"
value.literal: Emperor Ming covered his face against the bed and said, "If it is as you say, how could the Jin mandate again be long-lasting!"

value.zh: 迹其猜忍，蓋有符於狼顧也。
value.en: His cruelty matched wolf stare.
value.literal: Tracing his suspicious cruelty fits wolf-gaze omen.

value.zh: 制曰：夫天地之大，黎元為本；
value.en: Edict: realm rests on people;
value.literal: Decree says: Vast as Heaven and Earth—the common people are root;

value.zh: 邦國之貴，元首為先。
value.en: state treasures ruler.
value.literal: precious as state—sovereign comes first.

value.zh: 治亂無常，興亡有運。
value.en: Times turn—fate shifts.
value.literal: Order and chaos lack constancy—rise and fall have fortune.

value.zh: 是故五帝之上，居萬乘以為憂；
value.en: Five emperors ruled anxious;
value.literal: Therefore above Five Emperors—occupying myriad chariots they worried;

value.zh: 三王已來，處其憂而為樂。
value.en: three kings sought joy in care.
value.literal: since Three Kings—they dwelt in worry yet found joy.

value.zh: 競智力，爭利害，大小相吞，強弱相襲。
value.en: Brains and blades—swallow or be swallowed.
value.literal: Competed in wit and strength—contended profit—great swallowed small—strong struck weak.

value.zh: 逮乎魏室，三方鼎峙，干戈不息，氛霧交飛。
value.en: Wei era—three kingdoms—war-smoke.
value.literal: Down to Wei house—three corners tripod—spears unceasing—miasma flew crossed.

value.zh: 宣皇以天挺之姿，應期佐命，文以纘治，武以棱威。
value.en: Xuan paired mandate—civil weave—martial awe.
value.literal: Emperor Xuan with Heaven-endowed bearing answered period assisting mandate—literature to continue rule—military to grind awe.

value.zh: 用人如在己，求賢若不及；
value.en: He treated appointments like personal errands and chased worthy men as if always too late.
value.literal: Employing men as if himself—seeking worth as if falling short;

value.zh: 情深阻而莫測，性寬綽而能容。
value.en: His feelings ran dark and impossible to read; his manner stayed broad enough to absorb insult.
value.literal: emotion deep and obstructed unfathomable—nature broad yet containing.

value.zh: 和光同塵，與時舒卷，戢鱗潛翼，思屬風雲。
value.en: Merged dust—hid claws—waited storm.
value.literal: Blended gleam with dust—rolled with seasons—folded scales hid wings—thought attached wind cloud.

value.zh: 飾忠于已詐之心，延安于將危之命。
value.en: Feigned loyalty—bought time.
value.literal: Displayed loyalty from treacherous heart—extended peace with perilous mandate.

value.zh: 觀其雄略內斷，英猷外決，殄公孫於百日，擒孟達於盈旬，自以兵動若神，謀無再計矣。
value.en: Observe his inner heroic resolve and outer brilliant plans: he wiped out Gongsun in a hundred days and captured Meng Da within a full ten-day span; he thought his troop movements godlike and his stratagems in need of no second plan.
value.literal: Observe his heroic decisiveness within brilliant scheme without—extinguished Gongsun in hundred days—captured Meng Da within full ten-day span—self-thought soldier movement godlike—stratagem needed no second plan.

value.zh: 既而擁眾西舉，與諸葛相持。
value.en: West face Zhuge—stalemate.
value.literal: Yet massed hosts west rising—with Zhuge Liang stalemate.

value.zh: 抑其甲兵，本無鬭志，遺其巾幗，方發憤心。
value.en: Women’s ribbons—shame battle.
value.literal: Restrained armor weapons—originally lacked battle will—sent women’s scarves—then roused angry heart.

value.zh: 杖節當門，雄圖頓屈，請戰千里，詐欲示威。
value.en: When a staff of authority blocked the gate, his grand design was abruptly bent; requesting battle from a thousand li away, he feigned a wish to display might.
value.literal: Staff insignia blocked gate—grand plan abruptly bent—requested battle thousand li—feigned wishing display might.

value.zh: 且秦蜀之人，勇懦非敵，夷險之路，勞逸不同，以此爭功，其利可見。
value.en: Shu vs Wei terrain uneven odds.
value.literal: Moreover Qin-Shu people brave coward unmatched—barrier roads labor ease different—using this contest merit advantage visible.

value.zh: 而返閉軍固壘，莫敢爭鋒，生怯實而未前，死疑虛而猶遁，良將之道，失在斯乎！
value.en: Stalled behind walls—cowardice mistaken prudence!
value.literal: Yet returned closing army fortifying ramparts—none dared contend edge—alive cowardice solid yet not advancing—dead doubt empty yet still fleeing—good general’s way failure lies here!

value.zh: 文帝之世，輔翼權重，許昌同蕭何之委，崇華甚霍光之寄。
value.en: Regency rivaled Xiao He-Huo Guang.
value.literal: During Wen emperor’s reign wings authority heavy—Xuchang same as Xiao He’s commission—Chonghua deeper than Huo Guang’s trust.

value.zh: 當謂竭誠盡節，伊傅可齊。
value.en: Should match Yi Yin purity.
value.literal: Should have exhausted loyalty utmost fidelity—Yi Yin Fu Yue parallel.

value.zh: 及明帝將終，棟樑是屬，受遺二主，佐命三朝，既承忍死之託，曾無殉生之報。
value.en: Two deathbeds—three reigns—no martyr payment.
value.literal: When Ming emperor near end pillar beam entrusted—received testament two lords—aided mandate three courts—already undertook endure-death trust—never offered die-for-lord repayment.

value.zh: 天子在外，內起甲兵，陵土未乾，遽相誅戮，貞臣之體，寧若此乎！
value.en: Emperor absent—Luoyang coup—fresh tomb—bloodbath—loyalty?
value.literal: Son of Heaven outside—armor rose within—imperial mound earth not dry—suddenly mutual slaughter—upright minister’s bearing—could it be thus!

value.zh: 盡善之方，以斯為惑。
value.en: Perfection veils doubt.
value.literal: Perfect governance method—here lies confusion.

value.zh: 夫征討之策，豈東智而西愚？
value.en: Wise east foolish west?
value.literal: Could expedition strategy east wise west foolish?

value.zh: 輔佐之心，何前忠而後亂？
value.en: Same heart?
value.literal: Assistant heart why earlier loyal later turbulent?

value.zh: 故晉明掩面，恥欺偽以成功；
value.en: Ming hid eyes—shamed fraud victory;
value.literal: Therefore Jin Ming covered face—ashamed deceit achieving success;

value.zh: 石勒肆言，笑姦回以定業。
value.en: Shi Le mocked Jin hypocrisy.
value.literal: Shi Le unrestrained speech—laughed treacherous twist fixing enterprise.

value.zh: 古人有云，「積善三年，知之者少；
value.en: An ancient said, "Accumulate goodness for three years, and few know of it;
value.literal: An ancient said, "Accumulate goodness for three years, and few know of it;

value.zh: 為惡一日，聞于天下」，可不謂然乎！
value.en: do evil for one day, and it is heard throughout the world." Can this not be called true!
value.literal: do evil for one day, and it is heard throughout the world." Can this not be called true!

value.zh: 雖自隱過當年，而終見嗤後代。
value.en: Hidden sins mocked later.
value.literal: Although concealed faults that year—finally mocked later generations.

value.zh: 亦猶竊鍾掩耳，以眾人為不聞；
value.en: Like the bell thief plugging his ears—
value.literal: Also like stealing bell covering ears—thinking crowd hears not;

value.zh: 銳意盜金，謂市中為莫覩。
value.en: gold thief blind.
value.literal: keen stealing gold—thinking market blind.

value.zh: 故知貪于近者則遺遠，溺于利者則傷名；
value.en: Greed for what is near forfeits what is far;
value.literal: Thus know greed near abandons far—drowning profit harms name;

value.zh: 若不損己以益人，則當禍人而福己。
value.en: hurt others gain self.
value.literal: if not diminish self benefit others—then harm others bless self.

value.zh: 順理而舉易為力，背時而動難為功。
value.en: Move with the pattern and effort comes easily;
value.literal: Follow pattern raising easy force—oppose season moving hard merit.

value.zh: 況以未成之晉基，逼有餘之魏祚？
value.en: How much more when Jin’s foundation was still unbuilt and it pressed against a Wei mandate that yet had life in it?
value.literal: Moreover unfinished Jin foundation pressing ample Wei mandate?

value.zh: 雖復道格區宇，德被蒼生，而天未啟時，寶位猶阻，非可以智競，不可以力爭，雖則慶流後昆，而身終於北面矣。
value.en: Heaven withheld throne—died Wei subject.
value.literal: Although again Way spanning realm virtue covering dark-green generation—Heaven not yet opened hour treasure throne still blocked—not by wisdom compete—not by strength contend—although blessing flows later generations—person ended facing north.

value.zh: 都督雍梁二州諸軍事 據三國志魏志以下僅稱魏志、蜀志或吳志。
value.en: Commander of military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces. Based on Records of the Three Kingdoms, Wei zhi—hereafter cited only as Wei zhi, Shu zhi, or Wu zhi.
value.literal: Commanded Yong-Liang two provinces military affairs—according to Records of Three Kingdoms Wei

value.zh: 陳留王紀，梁州置於景元四年十二月，在此後三十餘年。
value.en: Annals of the Prince of Chenliu: Liang province was established in the twelfth month of the fourth year of Jingyuan, more than thirty years later than this.
value.literal: Prince of Chenliu annals—Liang province established twelfth month fourth year Jingyuan—more than thirty years later.

value.zh: 司馬懿督二州係代曹真，景初三年趙儼代懿，魏志曹真傳、趙儼傳都作「雍涼」。
value.en: Sima Yi's command over the two provinces followed his replacement of Cao Zhen; in the third year of Jingchu, Zhao Yan replaced Yi, and both the Wei zhi biographies of Cao Zhen and Zhao Yan write "Yong and Liang."
value.literal: Sima Yi's command over the two provinces followed his replacement of Cao Zhen; in the third year of Jingchu, Zhao Yan replaced Yi, and both the Wei zhi biographies of Cao Zhen and Zhao Yan write "Yong and Liang."

value.zh: 疑當從魏志。
value.en: Editors conclude the text should align with the Wei zhi.
value.literal: The doubtful passage ought to follow the Wei Records.

value.zh: 諡曰文後改諡宣文 各本皆作「諡曰文貞，後改諡文宣」。
value.en: For "posthumously named Wen and later changed to Xuanwen," all editions write "posthumously named Wenzhen and later changed to Wenxuan."
value.literal: For "posthumously named Wen and later changed to Xuanwen," all editions write "posthumously named Wenzhen and later changed to Wenxuan."

value.zh: 考異：「按禮志，魏朝初諡宣帝為文侯，景帝為武侯。
value.en: The Kaoyi says, "According to the Treatise on Rites, when the Wei court first gave posthumous names, Emperor Xuan was named Marquis Wen and Emperor Jing was named Marquis Wu.
value.literal: The Kaoyi says, "According to the Treatise on Rites, when the Wei court first gave posthumous names, Emperor Xuan was named Marquis Wen and Emperor Jing was named Marquis Wu.

value.zh: 文王表不宜與二祖同，於是改諡宣文、忠武。
value.en: King Wen memorialized that they should not be the same as the two ancestors, and therefore the posthumous names were changed to Xuanwen and Zhongwu.
value.literal: King Wen memorialized that they should not be the same as the two ancestors, and therefore the posthumous names were changed to Xuanwen and Zhongwu.

value.zh: 然則初諡文，無『貞』字也。
value.en: Thus the initial posthumous name was Wen, and did not have the graph 'zhen'.
value.literal: Thus the initial posthumous name was Wen, and did not have the graph 'zhen'.

value.zh: 禮志及文帝紀並稱舞陽宣文侯，宋書禮志同。
value.en: The Treatise on Rites and the Basic Annals of Emperor Wen both call him Marquis Xuanwen of Wuyang, and the Treatise on Rites in the Song shu is the same.
value.literal: The Treatise on Rites and the Basic Annals of Emperor Wen both call him Marquis Xuanwen of Wuyang, and the Treatise on Rites in the Song shu is the same.

value.zh: 此云『文宣』，亦轉寫之誤。」
value.en: Here saying 'Wenxuan' is also a copying error."
value.literal: Here saying 'Wenxuan' is also a copying error."

value.zh: 今據改。
value.en: Corrected per collation.
value.literal: Now emended accordingly.

value.zh: 景皇帝諱師，字子元，宣帝長子也。
value.en: Emperor Jing, whose personal name was Shi and courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan of Jin.
value.literal: Emperor Jing, taboo name Shi, courtesy name Ziyuan, was the eldest son of Emperor Xuan.

value.zh: 雅有風彩，沈毅多大略。
value.en: He carried himself with quiet distinction, steady and resolute, with a strategist’s breadth of mind.
value.literal: He had refined bearing and presence, was deep and resolute, and possessed great strategic vision.

value.zh: 少流美譽，與夏侯玄、何晏齊名。
value.en: While still young he was widely praised, and his name stood alongside those of Xiahou Xuan and He Yan.
value.literal: In youth he enjoyed a fine reputation, and was ranked with Xiahou Xuan and He Yan.

value.zh: 晏常稱曰：「惟幾也能成天下之務，司馬子元是也。」
value.en: He Yan used to say, "It takes someone who senses the moment before it turns to carry the weight of the realm—and that man is Sima Ziyuan."
value.literal: He Yan often declared, "Only one who apprehends subtle turning points can accomplish the affairs of all under Heaven; Sima Ziyuan is such a man."

value.zh: 魏景初中，拜散騎常侍，累遷中護軍。
value.en: During Wei’s Jingchu years he received appointment as Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and rose step by step to Central Protector of the Army.
value.literal: In the Jingchu era of Wei, he was appointed Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary and eventually promoted to Central Protector of the Army.

value.zh: 為選用之法，舉不越功，吏無私焉。
value.en: He set rules for appointments so that promotions matched real achievement, and his staff could not trade on personal connections.
value.literal: He established methods for selection and appointment; recommendations did not exceed actual merit, and clerks practiced no private favoritism.

value.zh: 宣穆皇后崩，居喪以至孝聞。
value.en: After Empress Dowager Xuanmu’s death, he kept mourning with such scrupulous grief that word of his filial piety spread everywhere.
value.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuanmu died, he observed mourning for her and was famed for extreme filial devotion.

value.zh: 宣帝之將誅曹爽，深謀秘策，獨與帝潛畫，文帝弗之知也。
value.en: As Sima Yi readied the strike against Cao Shuang, he laid his plans in the deepest secrecy—working them out alone with Sima Shi—while Sima Zhao was kept entirely in the dark.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan was about to execute Cao Shuang, with deep plots and secret stratagems he secretly planned only with the Emperor (Sima Shi); Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao) did not know of it.

value.zh: 將發夕乃告之，既而使人覘之，帝寢如常，而文帝不能安席。
value.en: Sima Yi waited until the night before the coup to inform his son; when he sent men to watch Sima Shi’s quarters, Shi slept soundly as on any other night, while Sima Zhao tossed and could not settle.
value.literal: On the eve of launching the action he was told; then someone was sent to spy on him—the Emperor slept as usual, but Emperor Wen could not find rest on his mat.

value.zh: 晨會兵司馬門，鎮靜內外，置陣甚整。
value.en: At daybreak he drew up his forces at the Sima Gate, steadying the palace inside and out and arraying them with flawless discipline.
value.literal: At dawn he assembled troops at the Sima Gate, calming inside and outside, and deployed formations in very good order.

value.zh: 宣帝曰：「此子竟可也。」
value.en: Sima Yi said, "This boy will do after all."
value.literal: Emperor Xuan said, "This son is indeed capable."

value.zh: 初，帝陰養死士三千，散在人間，至是一朝而集，眾莫知所出也。
value.en: Earlier, Sima Shi had quietly kept three thousand devoted fighters dispersed through the capital; now they materialized overnight, and no one could guess where they had sprung from.
value.literal: At the outset the Emperor had secretly maintained three thousand bravos, scattered among the people; at this moment they gathered in a single morning, and the multitude did not know whence they had come.

value.zh: 事平，以功封長平鄉侯，食邑千戶，尋加衛將軍。
value.en: After the coup succeeded he was rewarded with the village marquisate of Changping and a thousand-household fief, and before long was named General of the Guard as well.
value.literal: When the affair was settled, by merit he was enfeoffed as village marquis of Changping with a fief of one thousand households; soon he was additionally appointed General of the Guard.

value.zh: 及宣帝薨，議者咸云「伊尹既卒，伊陟嗣事」，天子命帝以撫軍大將軍輔政。
value.en: At Sima Yi’s death, court opinion echoed the old line—“When Yi Yin passed away, his son Yi Zhi carried on the task”—and the Wei emperor appointed Sima Shi General Who Pacifies the Army to assist in government.
value.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, those who deliberated all said, "After Yi Yin died, Yi Zhi succeeded to his duties," and the Son of Heaven ordered the Emperor as General Who Stabilizes the Army and Great General to assist in government.

value.zh: 魏嘉平四年春正月，遷大將軍，加侍中，持節、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。
value.en: In the first month of spring, Wei’s fourth year of Jiaping, he advanced to Great General, was given the concurrent post of Palace Attendant, received the imperial baton, took overall command of central and frontier forces, and assumed control of the Secretariat.
value.literal: In the first month of spring in the fourth year of Jiaping of Wei, he was promoted to Great General, added as Palace Attendant, bearing credentials, supervising all military affairs of the central command and the regions, and recording Director of the Secretariat business.

value.zh: 命百官舉賢才，明少長，恤窮獨，理廢滯。
value.en: He instructed every office to put forward able men, to sort seniority fairly, to relieve the widowed and alone, and to clear the backlog of neglected business.
value.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to recommend worthy talent, clarify precedence of young and old, show pity to the destitute and solitary, and straighten out stalled appointments.

value.zh: 諸葛誕、毌丘儉、王昶、陳泰、胡遵都督四方，王基、州泰、鄧艾、石苞典州郡，盧毓、李豐裳選舉，傅嘏、虞松參計謀，鐘會、夏侯玄、王肅、陳本、孟康、趙酆、張緝預朝議，四海傾注，朝野肅然。
value.en: Zhuge Dan, Guanqiu Jian, Wang Chang, Chen Tai, and Hu Zun held regional commands; Wang Ji, Zhou Tai, Deng Ai, and Shi Bao ran the provinces; Lu Yu and Li Feng handled personnel; Fu Gu and Yu Song shaped policy; Zhong Hui, Xiahou Xuan, Wang Su, Chen Ben, Meng Kang, Zhao Feng, and Zhang Ji sat in on the great councils. The empire fixed its hopes on them, and court and countryside grew solemn.
value.literal: Zhuge Dan, Guanqiu Jian, Wang Chang, Chen Tai, and Hu Zun supervised the four quarters; Wang Ji, Zhou Tai, Deng Ai, and Shi Bao administered prefectures and commanderies; Lu Yu and Li Feng oversaw selection and appointment; Fu Gu and Yu Song joined in planning stratagems; Zhong Hui, Xiahou Xuan, Wang Su, Chen Ben, Meng Kang, Zhao Feng, and Zhang Ji took part in court deliberations; the four seas turned their gaze upon them, and court and countryside stood in solemn awe.

value.zh: 或有請改易制度者，帝曰：「'不識不知，順帝之則'，詩人之美也。
value.en: When voices rose for sweeping institutional change, Sima Shi answered, "The Odes praise the ruler who does not meddle for show but simply follows the pattern Heaven set for the sage-kings.
value.literal: When some requested changes to institutions, the Emperor said: "'Not knowing, not perceiving, following the norms of the Di'—that is what the poets praise.

value.zh: 三祖典制，所宜遵奉；
value.en: The precedents left by the three Wei founders are what we are bound to honor;
value.literal: The regulations of the three founding ancestors are what ought to be obeyed and upheld;

value.zh: 自非軍事，不得妄有改革。」
value.en: and apart from what war demands, nothing should be changed on a whim."
value.literal: unless it be military affairs, one must not recklessly carry out reforms."

value.zh: 公卿將校皆詣府喻旨，帝以禮辭讓。
value.en: The high ministers and commanders crowded his gate with the edict; he declined again by formal courtesy.
value.literal: Dukes, ministers, generals, and colonels all went to the mansion to explain the intent; the Emperor by rite declined.

value.zh: 司空鄭沖率群官勸進曰：「伏見嘉命顯至，竊聞明公固讓，沖等眷眷，實有愚心。
value.en: Minister of Works Zheng Chong led the assembled officials in urging advancement, saying, "We humbly see that the fine command has manifestly arrived, and privately hear that your enlightened lordship firmly declines it. Chong and the others are full of concern and truly have a foolish thought.
value.literal: Minister of Works Zheng Chong led the assembled officials in urging advancement, saying, "We humbly see that the fine command has manifestly arrived, and privately hear that your enlightened lordship firmly declines it. Chong and the others are full of concern and truly have a foolish thought.

value.zh: 以為聖王作制，百代同風，褒德賞功，有自來矣。
value.en: The sage kings set precedent for every age: to honor merit is the way of antiquity itself.
value.literal: We consider that the sage king makes institutions; a hundred generations share one wind; praising virtue and rewarding merit has had its source from of old.

value.zh: 昔伊尹，有莘氏之媵臣耳，一佐成湯，遂荷阿衡之號。
value.en: Yi Yin began as a mere attendant of Youxin; one service to Tang won him the name Ah Heng.
value.literal: In the past Yi Yin was only Youxin's accompanying minister; once he assisted Cheng Tang, then he bore the title of Ah Heng.

value.zh: 周公藉已成之勢，據既安之業，光宅曲阜，奄有龜蒙。
value.en: The Duke of Zhou took power already won and a realm already calm, then made Qufu his seat and held Gui and Meng.
value.literal: The Duke of Zhou leaned on already completed power, occupied already secure enterprise, brightly dwelt at Qufu, covered Gui and Meng.

value.zh: 呂尚，磻溪之漁者也，一朝指麾，乃封營丘。
value.en: Lü Shang was a fisherman by Pan Creek; one morning’s command won him Yingqiu.
value.literal: Lü Shang was a fisherman of Panxi; one morning directing and waving, then was enfeoffed at Yingqiu.

value.zh: 自是以來，功薄而賞厚者，不可勝數，然賢哲之士，猶以為美談。
value.en: Since then thin merit has often drawn rich reward—yet wise men still praise those tales.
value.literal: From this onward, those whose merit was thin yet reward was thick cannot be counted; yet worthy and wise gentlemen still take them as fine tales.

value.zh: 況自先相國以來，世有明德，翼輔魏室，以綏天下，朝無秕政，人無謗言。
value.en: From the former Chancellor of State onward, each generation has aided Wei with shining virtue until the court is clean of chaff and the people free of slander.
value.literal: Moreover since the former Chancellor of State, generation after generation there has been bright virtue, winging and assisting the Wei house, thereby pacifying all under Heaven; court has no chaff government, men have no slanderous words.

value.zh: 前者明公西征靈州，北臨沙漠，榆中以西，望風震服，羌戎來馳，回首內向，東誅叛逆，全軍獨克。
value.en: You marched west to Lingzhou and north to the sands; west of Yuzhong every tribe trembled into submission; Qiang and Rong wheeled their horses toward the throne; in the east you cut down rebels alone and whole.
value.literal: Formerly the enlightened lord west campaigned Lingzhou, north faced the desert; west of Yuzhong, gazing at the wind trembled and submitted; Qiang and Rong came galloping, turned head inward; east punished rebels and traitors, whole army alone overcame.

value.zh: 禽闔閭之將，虜輕銳之卒以萬萬計，威加南海，名懾三越，宇內康寧，苛慝不作。
value.en: You took Wu’s generals and tens of thousands of their best troops, spread terror to the Southern Sea and the three Yues, and brought peace so that cruelty died away.
value.literal: Captured Helü's generals, took light keen soldiers by the ten thousands counted; awe added to South Sea, name overawed the three Yues; within the four seas peaceful and tranquil, harsh evil did not arise.

value.zh: 是以時俗畏懷，東夷獻舞。
value.en: The age stands in awe; even the eastern Yi send dancers to your court.
value.literal: Therefore the age's customs feared and cherished; eastern Yi presented dance.

value.zh: 故聖上覽乃昔以來禮典舊章，開國光宅，顯茲太原。
value.en: Therefore the sage Son of Heaven has weighed the old statutes and opened a bright fief for you at Taiyuan.
value.literal: Therefore the sage superior surveys thence past rites and canons, old regulations, opens state and bright dwelling, displays this Taiyuan.

value.zh: 明公宜承奉聖旨，受茲介福，允當天人。
value.en: You should accept the imperial word, take this great blessing, and satisfy both Heaven and the people.
value.literal: The enlightened lord ought to receive and follow the sage decree, receive this great blessing, truly meet Heaven and men.

value.zh: 元功盛勳，光光如彼；
value.en: Your founding merit shines so bright;
value.literal: Founding merit and blazing achievement, blazingly thus;

value.zh: 國土嘉祚，巍巍如此。
value.en: the fief and fortune offered you stand so high.
value.literal: State soil and fine blessing, thus lofty.

value.zh: 內外協同，靡愆靡違。
value.en: Within and without all move as one, without fault or breach.
value.literal: Inner and outer join in harmony; none fault, none violate.

value.zh: 由斯征伐，則可朝服濟江，掃除吳會，西塞江源，望祀岷山。
value.en: With that you may cross the Yangzi in court dress, sweep Wu clean, seal the river’s upper course, and offer the rite on Mount Min.
value.literal: From this campaigning, then can in court robes cross the Yangtze, sweep and clear Wu and Hui, west block Yangtze's source, gaze-sacrifice Mount Min.

value.zh: 回戈弭節，以麾天下，遠無不服，邇無不肅。
value.en: Then lay by spear and still the reins to command the realm until the far submit and the near stand in awe.
value.literal: Turn halberd and still the baton, thereby to command all under Heaven; far none not submit, near none not solemn.

value.zh: 令大魏之德，光于唐虞；
value.en: Great Wei’s virtue will outshine Tang and Yu;
value.literal: Let great Wei's virtue shine on Tang and Yu;

value.zh: 明公盛勳，超于桓文。
value.en: and your merit will rise above Huan and Wen.
value.literal: the enlightened lord's blazing merit surpasses Huan and Wen.

value.zh: 然後臨滄海而謝支伯，登箕山而揖許由，豈不盛乎！
value.en: Then you might stand by the eastern sea as kings of old did before worthy recluses, or climb Mount Ji to salute Xu You—what could be more glorious!
value.literal: Then facing the dark sea and thanking Zhibo, ascending Mount Ji and bowing to Xu You—is it not grand!

value.zh: 至公至平，誰與為鄰，何必勤勤小讓也哉。」
value.en: With utmost publicness and utmost fairness, who can be your neighbor? Why must you earnestly make this small refusal?"
value.literal: With utmost publicness and utmost fairness, who can be your neighbor? Why must you earnestly make this small refusal?"

value.zh: 帝乃受命。
value.en: Sima Zhao then accepted.
value.literal: The Emperor then received the command.

value.zh: 十一月，鄧艾帥萬餘人自陰平逾絕險至江由，破蜀將諸葛瞻於綿竹，斬瞻，傳首。
value.en: In the eleventh month Deng Ai took ten thousand men over the sheer track from Yinping to Jiangyou, crushed Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu, struck off his head, and sent it east by post.
value.literal: Eleventh month, Deng Ai led more than ten thousand from Yinping crossing extreme peril to reach Jiangyou, defeated Shu general Zhuge Zhan at Mianzhu, beheaded Zhan, sent the head by relay.

value.zh: 進軍雒縣，劉禪降。
value.en: He pushed on to Luo county, and Liu Shan yielded.
value.literal: Advanced the army to Luo county; Liu Shan surrendered.

value.zh: 天子命晉公以相國總百揆，於是上節傳，去侍中、大都督、錄尚書之號焉。
value.en: The emperor named the Duke of Jin chancellor with full authority over the government; Sima Zhao thereupon returned his batons and dropped the concurrent titles of Palace Attendant, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and overseer of the Secretariat.
value.literal: The Son of Heaven ordered the Duke of Jin by Chancellor of State to overall command the hundred handles; thereupon he submitted credentials and tallies, removed Palace Attendant, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and recording Director of the Secretariat titles.

value.zh: 表鄧艾為太尉，鐘會為司徒。
value.en: He recommended Deng Ai for Grand Commandant and Zhong Hui for Minister of Education.
value.literal: He memorialized Deng Ai as Grand Commandant, Zhong Hui as Minister of Education.

value.zh: 會潛謀叛逆，因密使譖艾。
value.en: Zhong Hui plotted revolt in secret and sent agents to traduce Deng Ai.
value.literal: Hui secretly plotted rebellion, thereby secretly sent to slander Ai.

value.zh: 咸熙元年春正月，檻車征艾。
value.en: In the first month of spring, Xianxi year 1, Deng Ai was summoned back in a prison cart.
value.literal: First year of Xianxi, spring, first month, caged cart summoned Ai.

value.zh: 乙丑，帝奉天子西征，次於長安。
value.en: On yichou he escorted the emperor west and encamped at Chang’an.
value.literal: On yichou, the Emperor escorting the Son of Heaven west campaigned, halted at Chang'an.

value.zh: 是時魏諸王侯悉在鄴城，命從事中郎山濤行軍司事，鎮於鄴，遣護軍賈充持節、督諸軍，據漢中。
value.en: With every Wei prince gathered at Yecheng, he put Shan Tao in charge of rear-area command there and sent Jia Chong with baton to oversee the armies holding Hanzhong.
value.literal: At this time Wei various princes and marquises were all at Yecheng; he ordered Retainer Shan Tao to conduct army affairs, garrisoning at Yecheng; sent Army Protector Jia Chong bearing credentials, supervising the various armies, occupying Hanzhong.

value.zh: 鐘會遂反於蜀，監軍衛瓘、右將軍胡烈攻會，斬之。
value.en: Zhong Hui rose in Shu; Wei Guan and Hu Lie struck him down and took his head.
value.literal: Zhong Hui then rebelled in Shu; Army Supervisor Wei Guan, General of the Right Hu Lie attacked Hui, beheaded him.

value.zh: 初，會之伐蜀也，西曹屬邵悌言於帝曰：「鐘會難信，不可令行。」
value.en: At first, when Zhong Hui was attacking Shu, Shao Ti, subordinate of the Western Bureau, said to Sima Zhao, "Zhong Hui is hard to trust; he must not be allowed to go."
value.literal: At first, when Zhong Hui was attacking Shu, Shao Ti, subordinate of the Western Bureau, said to Sima Zhao, "Zhong Hui is hard to trust; he must not be allowed to go."

value.zh: 帝笑曰：「取蜀如指掌，而眾人皆言不可，唯會與吾意同。
value.en: Sima Zhao had only smiled and said, "Shu will fall as easily as reading one’s palm, though everyone else doubted—only Zhong Hui shared my view.
value.literal: The Emperor smiled and said: "Taking Shu is like pointing at the palm; yet the host of men all say it cannot be done; only Hui and Our intent agree.

value.zh: 滅蜀之後，中國將士，人自思歸，蜀之遺黎，猶懷震恐，縱有異志，無能為也。」
value.en: After Shu fell, every northern soldier would pine for home and the Shu populace would still quake with fear—even if someone harbored treason, he could do nothing with it."
value.literal: After extinguishing Shu, central state's officers and soldiers, each person thinks of returning; Shu's surviving common people still cherish trembling fear; even if they had different intent, they have no ability to act.

value.zh: 卒如所量。
value.en: Events proved him exactly right.
value.literal: In the end it was as he had measured.

value.zh: 丙辰，帝至自長安。
value.en: On bingchen he returned from Chang’an to the capital.
value.literal: On bingchen, the Emperor arrived from Chang'an.

value.zh: 三月己卯，進帝爵為王，增封並前二十郡。
value.en: On jimao in the third month he was raised from duke to king with twenty commanderies in all, old grants and new.
value.literal: Third month, day jimao, advanced the Emperor's noble rank to king, increased fief together with the previous twenty commanderies.

value.zh: 夏五月癸未，天子追加舞陽宣文侯為晉宣王，舞陽忠武侯為晉景王。
value.en: On guiwei in the fifth month of summer the emperor posthumously raised Sima Yi to Prince Xuan of Jin and Sima Shi to Prince Jing of Jin.
value.literal: Summer, fifth month, day guiwei, the Son of Heaven posthumously added Wuyang Marquis Xuanwen as Jin King Xuan, Wuyang Marquis Zhongwu as Jin King Jing.

value.zh: 秋七月，帝奏司空荀顗定禮儀，中護軍賈充正法律，尚書僕射裴秀議官制，太保鄭沖總而裁焉。
value.en: In the seventh month of autumn he charged Xun Yi with the rites, Jia Chong with the laws, Pei Xiu with the bureaucracy, and Zheng Chong as coordinator over all.
value.literal: Autumn, seventh month, the Emperor memorialized Minister of Works Xun Yi to fix rites and ceremonies, Central Army Protector Jia Chong to rectify laws and statutes, Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Xiu to deliberate official system, Grand Guardian Zheng Chong overall to judge them.

value.zh: 始建五等爵。
value.en: He began the institution of the five orders of nobility.
value.literal: For the first time established the five ranks of nobility.

value.zh: 冬十月丁亥，奏遣吳人相國參軍徐劭、散騎常侍水曹屬孫彧使吳，喻孫皓以平蜀之事，致馬錦等物，以示威懷。
value.en: On dinghai in the tenth winter month he memorialized to send Xu Shao and Sun Yu—Wu natives in his service—to Wu with horses and brocade, to tell Sun Hao of Shu’s fall and to blend threat with kindness.
value.literal: Winter, tenth month, day dinghai, memorialized to send Wu man Chancellor of State Army Advisor Xu Shao, Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Water Bureau Subordinate Sun Yu as envoys to Wu, informing Sun Hao of the affair of pacifying Shu, presenting horses, brocade, and such objects, in order to show awe and cherishing.

value.zh: 丙午，天子命中撫軍新昌鄉侯炎為晉世子。
value.en: On bingwu the emperor named Sima Yan, the Central Stabilizing General and Marquis of Xinchang township, heir apparent of Jin.
value.literal: On bingwu, the Son of Heaven ordered Central General Who Stabilizes the Army, village marquis of Xinchang Yan, to be Jin heir apparent.

value.zh: 武皇帝諱炎，字安世，文帝長子也。
value.en: The emperor honored posthumously as Wu bore the personal name Yan and the courtesy name Anshi; he was the firstborn son of Emperor Wen (Sima Zhao).
value.literal: The Martial Emperor's taboo name was Yan, his style name Anshi; he was the eldest son of Emperor Wen.

value.zh: 寬惠仁厚，沈深有度量。
value.en: Broad-minded, humane, and gentle by nature, he was grave and self-contained, with the measured bearing of a true ruler.
value.literal: He was generous, kind, and humane in his magnanimity, deep and reserved, with breadth of mind.

value.zh: 魏嘉平中，封北平亭侯，歷給事中、奉車都尉、中壘將軍，加散騎常侍，累遷中護軍、假節。
value.en: During Wei’s Jiaping years he received the Beipingting marquisate and rose through a string of palace and guard posts—gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, cavalier attendant-in-ordinary—until he became central protector, bearing the credential staff.
value.literal: In the Jiaping era of Wei he was enfeoffed as marquis of Beipingting, then served successively as gentleman in attendance, commandant of the imperial chariots, general of the central rampart, with additional appointment as regular palace attendant of cavalier, and was repeatedly promoted to central protector with plenary authority.

value.zh: 迎常道鄉公於東武陽，遷中撫軍，進封新昌鄉侯。
value.en: At Dongwuyang he received the duke of Changdaoxiang, was named central commander of the army, and was promoted to marquis of Xinchang.
value.literal: He welcomed the duke of Changdaoxiang at Dongwuyang, was transferred to central commander of the army, and advanced to enfeoffment as marquis of Xinchang.

value.zh: 及晉國建，立爲世子，拜撫軍大將軍，開府、副貳相國。
value.en: When the Jin state was founded, he was established as heir apparent, appointed Great General Who Pacifies the Army with an office of his own, and made second-in-command assisting the Minister of State.
value.literal: When the state of Jin was founded he was established as heir apparent, appointed great general who pacifies the army with independent command, and served as deputy to the minister of state.

value.zh: 十二月丁亥，追尊宣帝廟曰高祖，景帝曰世宗，文帝曰太祖。
value.en: Dinghai: Xuan, Jing, and Wen received temple names Gaozu, Shizong, and Taizu.
value.literal: On the day dinghai of the twelfth month posthumous temple names were raised: emperor Xuan as Gaozu, emperor Jing as Shizong, emperor Wen as Taizu.

value.zh: 是月大疫，洛陽死者太半。
value.en: A plague carried off over half of Luoyang that month.
value.literal: That month a great pestilence struck; more than half died in Luoyang.

value.zh: 封裴頠爲鉅鹿公。
value.en: Pei Wei received the Julu ducal title.
value.literal: Pei Wei was enfeoffed as duke of Julu.

value.zh: 孝惠皇帝諱衷，字正度，武帝第二子也。
value.en: Emperor Hui, whose personal name was Sima Zhong and courtesy name Zhengdu, was Emperor Wu’s second son.
value.literal: The Filial and Kind Emperor, taboo name Zhong, courtesy name Zhengdu, was the second son of Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 泰始三年，立爲皇太子，時年九歲。
value.en: In 267, when he was nine years old, he was named heir apparent.
value.literal: In the third year of Taishi, he was established as crown prince; at the time he was nine sui.

value.zh: 太熙元年四月己酉，武帝崩。
value.en: In the fourth month of the first year of Taixi, on the day jiyou, Emperor Wu died.
value.literal: In the first year of Taixi, on the jiyou day of the fourth month, Emperor Wu died.

value.zh: 是日，皇太子即皇帝位，大赦，改元爲永熙。
value.en: That same day the heir apparent ascended the throne, ordered a general amnesty, and adopted the reign title Yongxi.
value.literal: That same day the crown prince assumed the imperial throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Yongxi.

value.zh: 尊皇后楊氏曰皇太后，立妃賈氏爲皇后。
value.en: Empress Yang was elevated to empress dowager, and his consort Lady Jia was installed as empress.
value.literal: The empress, Lady Yang, was honored as empress dowager; Consort Jia was established as empress.

value.zh: 夏四月辛卯，日有蝕之。
value.en: Another solar eclipse occurred on the xinmao day in the fourth month.
value.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the xinmao day, there was a solar eclipse.

value.zh: 癸巳，梁王肜、趙王倫矯詔廢賈后爲庶人，司空張華、尚書僕射裴頠皆遇害，侍中賈謐及黨與數十人皆伏誅。
value.en: On the guisi day Princes Xiong and Lun forged an edict that deposed Empress Jia; Zhang Hua and Pei Wei were killed, and Jia Mi with dozens of his partisans went to the execution ground.
value.literal: On the guisi day, Prince Xiong of Liang and Prince Lun of Zhao forged an edict deposing Empress Jia to commoner status; Minister of Works Zhang Hua and Vice Director of the Secretariat Pei Wei both met harm and died; Palace Attendant Jia Mi and several tens of his faction were all executed.

value.zh: 甲午，倫矯詔大赦，自爲相國、都督中外諸軍，如宣文輔魏故事，追復故皇太子位。
value.en: The next day Prince Lun forged a general amnesty, named himself chancellor and commander-in-chief on the model of Sima Yi and Sima Zhao, and posthumously reinstated the murdered crown prince.
value.literal: On the jiawu day, Lun forged an edict for a general amnesty, made himself chancellor of state and area commander for all military affairs within and without, according to the old precedent of Xuan and Wen assisting Wei, and posthumously restored the former crown prince’s position.

value.zh: 丁酉，以梁王肜爲太宰，左光祿大夫何劭爲司徒，右光祿大夫劉寔爲司空，淮南王允爲驃騎將軍。
value.en: Prince Xiong became grand steward, He Shao minister of education, Liu Shi minister of works, and Prince Yun of Huainan general of agile cavalry on the dingyou day.
value.literal: On the dingyou day, Prince Xiong of Liang was made grand steward; Left Household Grandee He Shao was made minister of education; Right Household Grandee Liu Shi was made minister of works; Prince Yun of Huainan was made general of agile cavalry.

value.zh: 己亥，趙王倫矯詔害賈庶人于金墉城。
value.en: On the jihai day Prince Lun had the deposed Empress Jia killed inside the Jinyong fortress.
value.literal: On the jihai day, Prince Lun of Zhao forged an edict and harmed the commoner Jia at the Jinyong Fortress.

value.zh: 元皇帝諱睿，字景文，宣帝曾孫，琅邪恭王覲之子也。
value.en: Emperor Yuan, whose personal name was Rui and courtesy name Jingwen, was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan of Jin and the son of Sima Jin, Prince Gong of Langye.
value.literal: The Emperor Yuan's taboo name was Rui, his courtesy name Jingwen; he was a great-grandson of Emperor Xuan and the son of Jin, Prince Gong of Langye.

value.zh: 咸寧二年生於洛陽，有神光之異，一室盡明，所藉槁如始刈。
value.en: He was born in Luoyang in 276, amid a strange glow that lit the whole chamber and left the bedding straw looking freshly mown.
value.literal: In the second year of Xianning he was born in Luoyang; there was a divine radiance anomaly; one room was entirely bright; the straw on which he lay was as if newly cut.

value.zh: 及長，白豪生於日角之左，隆準龍顏，目有精曜，顧眄煒如也。
value.en: As a man he bore a white filament beside the auspicious bump on his forehead, the high-bridged "dragon" profile of a ruler, and eyes so bright that every turn of his gaze seemed to flash with light.
value.literal: When grown, a white hair grew to the left of his sun-corner; high bridge nose and dragon countenance; his eyes had refined brilliance; his glances were radiant.

value.zh: 年十五，嗣位琅邪王。
value.en: At fifteen he inherited the title of Prince of Langye.
value.literal: At age fifteen he succeeded to the position of Prince of Langye.

value.zh: 幼有令問。
value.en: Even as a boy he was already known for an excellent name.
value.literal: In youth he had a fine reputation.

value.zh: 及惠皇之際，王室多故，帝每恭儉退讓，以免於禍。
value.en: Under Emperor Hui, when the house of Jin was rocked by one crisis after another, he habitually kept to modesty, frugality, and deference so as to stay clear of disaster.
value.literal: When it came to the time of Emperor Hui, the royal house had many troubles; the emperor each time was respectful, frugal, yielding, in order to avoid calamity.

value.zh: 沈敏有度量，不顯灼然之迹，故時人未之識焉。
value.en: He was steady, astute, and large-minded, yet never advertised his abilities, so his contemporaries failed to see the ruler in him.
value.literal: Deep and keen, with capacity for tolerance, he did not display glaring traces; therefore people of the time did not recognize him.

value.zh: 惟侍中嵇紹異之，謂人曰：「琅邪王毛骨非常，殆非人臣之相也。」
value.en: Only Ji Shao, the palace attendant, saw something different in him and told others, "The Prince of Langye has a presence no ordinary man possesses; that is hardly the look of someone born to serve another."
value.literal: Only Attendant-in-ordinary Ji Shao thought him strange, saying to people: "The Prince of Langye's bearing is extraordinary; probably it is not the appearance of a subject."

value.zh: 初，《玄石圖》有「牛繼馬後」，故宣帝深忌牛氏，遂爲二榼，共一口，以貯酒焉，帝先飲佳者，而以毒酒鴆其將牛金。
value.en: The Dark Stone Chart once warned that "an ox would follow the horse"; Emperor Xuan therefore feared the Niu surname, set out paired flasks with a single spout, drank the good wine himself, and poisoned his general Niu Jin from the other.
value.literal: Formerly, in the Dark Stone Chart there was "the ox follows the horse"; therefore Emperor Xuan deeply dreaded the Niu clan; then made two flasks, sharing one mouth, to store wine therein; the emperor first drank the fine, but with poisoned wine zhenned his general Niu Jin.

value.zh: 而恭王妃夏侯氏竟通小吏牛氏而生元帝，亦有符云。
value.en: Yet Lady Xiahou, consort of King Gong, took up with a minor clerk surnamed Niu and bore Emperor Yuan—another omen fulfilled, men said.
value.literal: Yet King Gong's consort Lady Xiahou in the end connected with clerk Niu and bore Yuan Emperor; there was also a tally saying so.

value.zh: 史臣曰：晉氏不虞，自中流外，五胡扛鼎，七廟隳尊，滔天方駕，則民懷其舊德者矣。
value.en: The historians write: Jin could not guard against calamity from within; beyond the heartland the Five Hu seized the cauldron, the imperial shrines were cast down, and rebellion rose like a flood—so the people clung to the memory of better days.
value.literal: The historians say: The Jin clan did not foresee it; from midstream outward, the five Hu shouldered the tripod, the seven temples toppled their honor; flooding Heaven side by side—then the people cherished its old virtue.

value.zh: 昔光武以數郡加名，元皇以一州臨極，豈武宣餘化猶暢于琅邪，文景垂仁傳芳于南頓，所謂後乎天時，先諸人事者也。
value.en: Guangwu rose from a handful of commanderies, while Emperor Yuan ruled from a single province—perhaps the lingering influence of King Wu and Emperor Xuan still flowed at Langye, and the kindness of Han Wendi and Jingdi still lingered at Nandun: fate came late, but human effort came first.
value.literal: Formerly Guangwu by several commanderies added fame; Yuan Huang by one province faced the extreme—was it that Wu and Xuan's remaining transformation still flowed at Langye, Wen and Jing's hanging benevolence transmitted fragrance at Nandun—what is called behind Heaven's timing, ahead of the multitude of human affairs.

value.zh: 馳章獻號，高蓋成陰，星斗呈祥，金陵表慶。
value.en: Memorials flew in offering the throne, noble coaches crowded the roads like a forest, the stars showed blessing, and Jinling proclaimed good fortune.
value.literal: Galloping memorials presented titles; high canopies became shade; stars and constellations showed auspice; Jinling displayed celebration.

value.zh: 陶士行擁三州之旅，郢外以安；
value.en: Tao Kan held three provinces' troops and the country beyond Jing grew calm;
value.literal: Tao Shixing embraced three provinces' hosts; outside Ying thereby was pacified;

value.zh: 王茂弘爲分陝之計，江東可立。
value.en: Wang Dao laid plans like the ancient "divided Shaan" partnership, and the lower Yangzi could stand as a realm.
value.literal: Wang Maohong made the divided-Shaan plan; east of the river could be established.

value.zh: 或高旌未拂，而遐心斯偃，回首朝陽，仰希乾棟，帝猶六讓不居，七辭而不免也。
value.en: Before his banners had swept the north, distant hearts already bowed; all eyes turned to the rising sun and looked for a pillar of state—yet even after six refusals of the throne and seven pleas to be spared, he could not escape taking it.
value.literal: Perhaps high banners not yet waved, yet distant hearts thereby lay low; turning the head toward the morning sun, looking up hoping for the Qian ridgepole—yet the emperor still six times yielded not to dwell, seven times declined yet could not avoid.

value.zh: 布帳綀帷，詳刑簡化，抑揚前軌，光啓中興。
value.en: Plain curtains and gauze screens, careful justice and lean government—he trimmed the excesses of the past and lit the torch of the restoration.
value.literal: Cloth curtains and pongee hangings; detailed punishments, simplified transformation; suppressing and raising former tracks, broadly opening restoration.

value.zh: 古首私家不蓄甲兵，大臣不爲威福，王之常制，以訓股肱。
value.en: The ancients said that private houses must not hoard arms and that ministers must not wield arbitrary power—such is the king's standing rule for teaching his servants.
value.literal: From of old it has been said: private families do not store armor and weapons; great ministers do not make awesomeness and fortune—this is the king's constant regulation, whereby to instruct thigh and arm.

value.zh: 中宗失馭強臣，自亡齊斧，兩京胡羯，風埃相望。
value.en: Zhongzong failed to bridle mighty vassals and so lost the regal axe himself; the twin capitals fell to Hu and Jie, and dust of war stretched from plain to plain.
value.literal: Zhongzong lost control of strong ministers, himself lost the Qi axe; two capitals Hu and Jie, wind and dust face each other.

value.zh: 雖復《六月》之駕無聞，而《鴻雁》之歌方遠，享國無幾，哀哉！
value.en: He never heard the war-chariots of the "Sixth Month" ode, and the lament of "Wild Geese" still rang far off; his reign was brief—how pitiful!
value.literal: Although again the "Sixth Month" chariot was unheard of, yet the "Wild Geese" song was still distant; enjoying the state not many—alas!

value.zh: 月五星犯列舍經星變附見
value.en: The Moon and the Five Planets Transgressing the Lodges and Classical Stars, with Supplementary Notes on Celestial Portents.
value.literal: Transgressions of the Moon and the Five Planets against the Lodges and Classical Stars; appended observations on anomalies.

value.zh: 魏文帝黃初四年三月癸卯，月犯心大星。
value.en: On guimao in the third month of Huangchu 4 under Emperor Wen of Wei (Cao Pi), the moon transgressed Antares, the bright star of the Heart mansion.
value.literal: In the third month of the fourth Huangchu year of Emperor Wen of Wei, on the day guimao, the Moon transgressed the great star of the Heart [lodge].

value.zh: 占曰：「心為天王位，王者惡之。」
value.en: The prognostication reads: “The Heart asterism marks Heaven’s throne—sovereigns dread such a sign.”
value.literal: The omen-text says: “The Heart is the seat of the Celestial King; the king finds it ill-omened.

value.zh: 六月甲申，太白晝見。
value.en: In the sixth month, on jiashen, Venus appeared in broad daylight.
value.literal: In the sixth month, on the day jiashen, the Great White [Venus] was seen in daytime.

value.zh: 案劉向《五紀論》曰：「太白少陰，弱，不得專行，故以己未為界，不得經天而行。
value.en: Examining Liu Xiang’s Treatise on the Five Regulators, it says, "Venus is Lesser Yin; being weak, it cannot travel independently. Therefore it takes jiwei as the boundary and may not cross the sky in its course.
value.literal: Investigating [this], Liu Xiang’s “Treatise on the Five Regulators” says: “The Great White is Lesser Yin; being weak, it cannot travel alone; therefore with jiwei as the boundary, it must not cross the sky [by day].

value.zh: 經天則晝見，其占為兵喪，為不臣，為更王；
value.en: If it crosses the sky, then it appears by day; its prognostication is war and mourning, disloyal ministers, and a changed king;
value.literal: When it crosses the sky, then it is seen by day; its interpretation is military losses, disloyal subjects, and change of king;

value.zh: 強國弱，小國強。」
value.en: strong states become weak, and small states become strong."
value.literal: strong states weaken, small states strengthen.

value.zh: 是時孫權受魏爵號，而稱兵距守。
value.en: Sun Quan had accepted Wei’s patent of nobility yet still mobilized armies and stood on the defensive.
value.literal: At this time Sun Quan accepted titles from Wei, yet raised troops and held out on the defensive.

value.zh: 其十二月丙子，月犯心大星。
value.en: In the twelfth month, on bingzi, the moon again crossed Antares in the Heart.
value.literal: That twelfth month, on the day bingzi, the Moon transgressed the great star of the Heart.

value.zh: 占同上。
value.en: The diviners cited the same gloss as above.
value.literal: The interpretation is the same as above.

value.zh: 五年十月乙卯，太白晝見。
value.en: In the tenth month of Huangchu 5, on yimao, Venus appeared in daylight.
value.literal: In the fifth year, tenth month, on the day yimao, the Great White was seen in daytime.

value.zh: 占同上。
value.en: The prognostication matched the foregoing.
value.literal: The interpretation is the same as above.

value.zh: 又歲星入太微逆行，積百四十九日乃出。
value.en: Jupiter also entered the Supreme Palace and traced a retrograde arc, lingering one hundred forty-nine days before departing.
value.literal: Moreover the Year Star [Jupiter] entered the Supreme Palace enclosure and moved retrograde; it accumulated one hundred forty-nine days there before emerging.

value.zh: 占曰：「五星入太微，從右入三十日以上，人主有大憂。」
value.en: The gloss runs: “If the five planets enter the Supreme Palace from the right and remain upward of thirty days, the sovereign faces grave distress.”
value.literal: The omen-text says: “When the Five Planets enter the Supreme Palace, entering from the right and staying thirty days or more, the ruler has great sorrow.

value.zh: 一曰：「有赦至。」
value.en: A variant reading adds: “A general amnesty is coming.”
value.literal: Another saying: “An amnesty will arrive.

value.zh: 七年五月，帝崩，明帝即位，大赦天下。
value.en: In the fifth month of the seventh year the emperor died; Emperor Ming took the throne and issued an empire-wide amnesty.
value.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year the emperor died; Emperor Ming succeeded and proclaimed a great amnesty for all under Heaven.

value.zh: 六年五月壬戌，熒惑入太微，至壬申，興歲星相及，俱犯右執法，至癸酉乃出。
value.en: On renxu in the fifth month of the sixth year Mars entered the Supreme Palace; by renshen it had closed with Jupiter, both crossing the Right Enforcer asterism, and they exited on guiyou.
value.literal: In the sixth year, fifth month, on the day renxu, Spark-Delight [Mars] entered the Supreme Palace; by renshen it came together with the Year Star [Jupiter], both transgressing the Right Enforcer; on guiyou they emerged.

value.zh: 占曰：「從右入三十日以上，人主有大憂。」
value.en: The interpretation states: “Remaining from the right beyond thirty days brings great sorrow to the sovereign.”
value.literal: The omen-text says: “Entering from the right and staying thirty days or more, the ruler has great sorrow.

value.zh: 又曰：「月、五星犯左右執法，大臣有憂。」
value.en: It also said, "When the moon or the five planets trespass against the Left or Right Enforcer, great ministers will have anxiety."
value.literal: It also says: “When the Moon or the Five Planets transgress the Left or Right Enforcer, great ministers have sorrow.

value.zh: 一曰：「執法者誅，金、火尤甚。」
value.en: A further gloss adds that “execution reaches the officials who ‘enforce the law,’ worst when Venus or Mars is involved.”
value.literal: Another saying: “The enforcers are executed; metal and fire [planets] make it especially severe.

value.zh: 十一月，皇子東武陽王鑒薨。
value.en: In the eleventh month the imperial son, Prince Jian of Dongwuyang, passed away.
value.literal: In the eleventh month the imperial son, Prince Jian of Dongwuyang, died.

value.zh: 七年正月，驃騎將軍曹洪免為庶人。
value.en: The following first month General of Agile Cavalry Cao Hong was stripped of rank and reduced to common status.
value.literal: In the first month of the seventh year Cao Hong, General of Agile Cavalry, was dismissed and made a commoner.

value.zh: 四月，征南大將軍夏侯尚薨。
value.en: In the fourth month Xiahou Shang, general who conquered the south, died.
value.literal: In the fourth month Xiahou Shang, General Who Conquers the South, died.

value.zh: 五月，帝崩。
value.en: In the fifth month the emperor died.
value.literal: In the fifth month the emperor died.

value.zh: 《蜀記》稱明帝問黃權曰：「天下鼎立，何地為正？」
value.en: The Records of Shu says that Emperor Ming asked Huang Quan, "With the realm standing like a tripod, which land is legitimate?"
value.literal: The “Records of Shu” relates that Emperor Ming asked Huang Quan: “The realm stands tripod-wise—which region holds the true legitimacy?

value.zh: 對曰：「當驗天文。
value.en: Quan replied, "It should be verified by celestial patterns.
value.literal: He replied: “One must verify it against astronomy.

value.zh: 往者熒惑守心而文帝崩，吳、蜀無事，此其徵也。」
value.en: Formerly Mars guarded Heart and Emperor Wen collapsed, while Wu and Shu had no incident; this is the proof."
value.literal: Formerly Spark-Delight stationed at the Heart and Emperor Wen died, yet Wu and Shu were untroubled—this was its proof.

value.zh: 案三國史並無熒惑守心之文，疑是入太微。
value.en: Scrutiny shows none of the Three Kingdoms annals records Mars ‘stationing at the Heart’; the event was probably entry into the Supreme Palace.
value.literal: Investigating the histories of the three states, there is no text of Spark-Delight stationing at the Heart; it is suspected that [the planet] entered the Supreme Palace.
